articleTitle: Securing Federated Learning: A Defense Mechanism Against Model Poisoning Threats
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Distributed machine learning advancements have the potential to transform future networking systems and communications. An effective framework for machine learning has been made possible by the introduction of Federated Learning (FL) and due to its decentralized nature it has some poisoning issues. Model poisoning attacks are one of them that significantly affect FL’s performance. Model poisoning mainly defines the replacement of a functional model with a poisoned model by injecting poison into models in the training period. The model’s boundary typically alters in some way as a result of a poisoning attack, which leads to unpredictability in the model outputs. Federated learning provides a mechanism to unleash data to fuel new AI applications by training AI models without access anyone’s confidential data. Currently, there are many algorithms that are being used for defending model poisoning in federated learning. Some of them are really efficient but most of them have lots of issues that don’t make the federated learning system properly secured. So in this study, we have highlighted the main issues of these algorithms and provided a defense mechanism that is capable of defending model poisoning in federated learning.

articleTitle: A Mixed Integer Linear Programming based optimal operational and sizing approach for a Hybrid Local Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Optimal sizing of microgrids is achieving higher importance in the current era of energy transition driven by renewable sources. Due to the intermittence of the renewable sources i.e. PV, wind assisted by energy storages i.e. battery the optimal sizing of the microgrids alonf with cost minimization is a great challenge. This study presents a methodological framework for determining the optimal configuration of a hybrid microgrid, integrating various energy resources such as photovoltaic (PV) generation, battery storage, a genset, and grid interconnection. Employing Pyomo optimization tool with a mixed-integer linear programming algorithm, the research focuses on sizing components within a 20 kW PV microgrid. Through meticulous examination of load demand and installed PV capacity, the algorithm strategically optimizes the sizing of PV panels, batteries, gensets, and grid interactions to minimize both capital expenditure (CAPEX) and operational expenditure (OPEX). The microgrid's performance is analyzed under three pricing schemes: net metering, selling excess energy to the grid (selling price less than buying price), and giving it away (zero price). Additionally, in off-grid mode, the total CO2 emissions are minimized. The proposed methodology offers a systematic approach for designing economically viable and efficient hybrid microgrids, essential for sustainable energy systems.

articleTitle: Unravel News: An Efficient Summarization Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The process of automatically creating a concise and informative summary of a news piece is known as news summarizing. This can be a useful tool for people who want to quickly get the gist of a news story without having to read the entire article. Extractive and abstractive summarization are the two basic methods used to summarize news. The process of extractive summarization entails locating and separating the key phrases from the source text. In this paper, sentence weighting is used for extractive summarization. The words in the headlines are given ten times more emphasis than the other words in the news article. The final summarization is done by rearranging the sentences as per the sequence in the main news article. The paper concludes by discussing the future of news summarization, which is an active area of research.

articleTitle: Modified Best Fit Algorithm for Reducing Power Consumption of 5G C-RAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The mobile network of the future generation face a difficult task due to the exponential increase in data traffic over time. It is anticipated that the cloud radio access network (C-RAN), a newly developed cellular network, will successfully address that difficulty. The primary distinction between the C-RAN and the conventional cellular architecture is the centralized baseband unit pool where baseband units (BBUs) are gathered to provide statistical multiplexing gains. In order to fully benefit from the C-RAN, it is necessary to apply effective optimization algorithm to develop network performance. Hence, in this paper, an algorithm called modified best fit to optimize BBU reconfiguration to the appropriate Remote Radio Heads (RRHs). According to the results, the proposed C-RAN outperforms the conventional network in terms of reducing the number of active BBUs and power consumption.

articleTitle: Multi-Head Self-Attention Mechanisms in Vision Transformers for Retinal Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a serious condition that can lead to eyesight loss in those who have diabetes if not identified early. The traditional diagnosis approach relies on the manual scrutiny of retinal images by specialists, a process that can be both time-consuming and susceptible to errors. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to revolutionize this field by providing automated, precise, and rapid identification of diabetic retinopathy (DR). In our study, we utilized Vision Transformers (ViTs) to achieve effective classification of retinal images. ViTs are advanced models that divide images into patches and utilize multi-head self-attention approaches to identify important features. The model demonstrated outstanding achievement, with a success rate of 96.13%, precision of 0.92, recall of 0.95, F1 score of 0.93, and ROC- AUC score of 0.969. The results of this study have significant implications for improving the detection of DR, enabling timely intervention, and potentially safeguarding the vision of a large number of individuals. Future research will focus on improving the resilience of the model by incorporating a wider range of datasets and optimizing its integration with medical procedures to ensure dependable and efficient performance in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Developing a Model for Predicting Multiple Sclerosis Progression Using MRI Scans
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: A significant number of people lose their lives to multiple sclerosis each year, and many of these victims come from rural areas. However, the technology for early sclerosis diagnosis is not as effective as anticipated. So, we set out to develop a solid method that can aid medical experts in diagnosing sclerosis. Despite a large body of research on the subject, we attempted to create a far more accurate and error-free classification method that is trained on a substantial amount of real datasets as opposed to augmented data. The network performs noticeably well on 15,600 MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) pictures using a modified Inception-v3, Resnet50, and Efficient Net. We found the enhanced InceptionV3 excelled, achieving 92.44% training, and 93.26% validation. Additionally, it outperformed several alternative CNN architectures already in use.

articleTitle: Harnessing CNN Architecture for Accurate Traffic Sign Classification: Findings from the GTSRB Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Traffic signs are vital components of road infrastructure, serving as visual cues that communicate essential information to drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists. They play a crucial role in maintaining road safety by guiding traffic, indicating hazards, and regulating speed limits and right-of-way. Additionally, traffic signs help to establish order and predictability on the roads, reducing the likelihood of accidents and promoting smooth traffic flow. The importance of traffic sign classification lies in its ability to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of sign recognition systems, contributing to safer driving environments and the development of intelligent transportation systems. In this research we have taken the GTSRB - German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark dataset and included 516 more images in the dataset. After some preprocessing steps, we split the dataset into train and test data. Finally, we have trained the data with GRU, VGG-16, VGG-19, and scratch CNN architecture. Accuracies found are 91.91%, 87.19%, 86.53%, and 99.62%.

articleTitle: Profit Demand Delegated Proof of Stake: Hypothetical Design Concept for Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS) is indeed a fascinating consensus algorithm used on various blockchain platforms. It was designed to address some of the scalability and energy consumption issues associated with Proof of Work (PoW) while maintaining decentralization to a certain extent. But, DPoS has some disadvantages in the distribution of profit share for stake forwarding nodes to delegate nodes. The profit share is controlled by the delegate nodes rather than the staking nodes or token holder voting nodes. Here, in Profit Demand Delegated Proof of Stake (PD-DPoS), we introduced a new mechanism to facilitate the token holder voting nodes to demand a rate of profit/profit share. PD-DPoS will encourage the delegate nodes to invest in infrastructure for high connectivity and fast computing crypto systems. As the system builds targeting fast and reliable computing by extending the opportunity of demanding profit share for token holder voter nodes will experimentally perform and prove better than the DPoS.

articleTitle: Computer Vision-based Interactive Autism Detection System using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a multifaceted neurodevelopmental disorder that influences communication, language abilities, and social interactions, affecting both verbal and nonverbal exchanges. Identifying and diagnosing ASD at an early stage is essential for creating timely educational strategies, providing family assistance, and ensuring suitable medical care is available. Early screening can facilitate the development of optimal therapeutic strategies at the right time. By analyzing facial features, significant markers encoded in human faces can be studied to identify ASD. In this research, we gathered facial images of children with ASD from publicly available sources and employed deep-learning classifiers to sort them. Furthermore, the classifier was utilized to differentiate various ASD subgroups, relying exclusively on the autistic image data. The need for automated diagnosis techniques for ASD has become increasingly important.To address this, we made use of a dataset containing 2,940 facial images of children with autism and those who are typically developing. We evaluated the outcomes of existing methods and enhanced the VGG16 model to improve its training and fitting processes. Through substantial modifications to variables such as epoch number and batch size, we increased the accuracy from 77% to 86.3%, while also calculating metrics like precision, specificity, and sensitivity. Moreover, we optimized the training and testing procedures compared to the base code. To enhance the evaluation of the results, we calculated several metrics, such as true positive, true negative, false positive, and false negative rates, in addition to accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and specificity. These results were documented in the submissions.csv file. Additionally, we implemented the VGG19 CNN model and compared its performance with VGG16. The deep learning approach achieved the highest accuracy of 88% with VGG19, followed by 86.3% with VGG16.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Systems for Detecting Hate Speech and Offensive Language in Texts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The critical work of recognizing hate speech and objectionable language on social media is essential to ensuring the safety of the online community. The usefulness of deep learning systems in recognizing such content is investigated in this work. Using regular expression replacement, lowercase conversion, stopword removal, stemming, and tokenization, we pre-processed a dataset of 24,783 tweets that were categorized as hate speech, offensive language, or neither. For training and testing, we divide the data using word embedding techniques. Numerous DL models, including CNN-LSTM, CNN-BiLSTM, LSTM, and BiLSTM fusion models, were used in the study. The BiLSTM model obtains a maximum accuracy of 90.54% in comparison to other models. A comparison examination with multiple data splits validates the robustness and practicality of our method. Our study’s findings show that BiLSTM models can reliably distinguish between hate speech and provocative language. This is advantageous for social media networks that use automatic content control.

articleTitle: Clustering-Based User Knowledge Extraction Structure for Furniture Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Furniture, a part of our daily lives, is designed in various forms and textures according to users' needs. Differences in furniture designs directly impact users' feelings and, therefore, their experiences with the product. The card sorting technique is one of the user experience research methods. This method is used to create mind maps of users towards a product. This study investigates user knowledge structure for furniture designs using card sorting and hierarchical cluster analysis methods. Card sorting data reveals patterns in how user experience designers categorize the semantic words users select for furniture designs through hierarchical cluster analysis. Hierarchical clustering, a popular data analysis method, has been used to detect semantic or contextual similarities and relationships of semantic words. Dendrogram diagrams were created using the hierarchical clustering method. With dendrogram diagrams, the relationship between the semantic word data related to furniture, how they are clustered, and how the clusters are grouped at lower and upper levels are examined. Thus, it helps designers to develop more optimal, user-centered product design. In this study, after the semantic space of 102 semantic words used in furniture comfort design was created, it was reduced to 35 words by the brainstorming method. Then, the semantic words were clustered using the hierarchical clustering algorithm by applying the card sorting technique to 69 participants. According to the results obtained, the rankings for furniture designs are clustered under five clusters: beautiful - ugly, multifunctional - single function, elegant - coarse, living - nonliving, and rough - smooth. The study provided data that designers can use to redesign furniture in a user-centered way.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of YouTube Comments Using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The extensive user engagement on YouTube leads to a flood of comments, creating challenges for content creators who aim to understand audience sentiment. Previous studies have mainly concentrated on distinguishing between positive, negative, and neutral sentiments in comments. This study involves creating a dataset of YouTube comments and classifying them into positive, negative, interrogative, corrective, imperative, and neutral categories, which will help content creators visualize other sentiments alongside positive, negative, and neutral sentiments. Based on the sentiment, they can improve their content and also enhance user interaction. Six machine learning algorithms—Naive Bayes (NB), Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Support Vector Machine (SVM)—are applied, with the SVM model demonstrating outstanding accuracy, reaching 94%.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches for Head and Neck Cancer Stage Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: One of the leading causes of death in the world is cancer. The stage detection of Head and Neck Cancer (HNC) is crucial because it influences the appropriate course of treatment at the appropriate moment, enhancing patient outcomes. The primary goal of this study is to determine the scope and seriousness accurately of the HNC. To assess the severity of HNC at four distinct phases, this study included a comprehensive analysis of a machine learning-based categorization system. In this study, advanced machine learning, more specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are used to detect the stage of severity of HNC. With a remarkable 99.76% accuracy rate, the CNN model performs better than VGG-16, VGG-19, ResNet50, and MobileNetV2 in the prediction of HNC staging. The model is beneficial for clinical workflows and helps researchers and medical professionals to make decisions more quickly and accurately in practical use.

Index Terms: Head And Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

articleTitle: Automated Leukemia Detection from Blood Samples using Machine Learning in MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Blood cancer is known as hematologic cancer, and leukemia is a type of blood cancer that infects the body’s white blood cells and bone marrow, leading to a painful death. This paper introduces an automatic technique for detecting leukemia using image processing techniques such as histogram equalization, linear contrast adjustment, and segmentation methods, including k-means clustering, marker-controlled watershed, and HSV color-based segmentation. We achieved 99.01% accuracy using CNN, Decision Tree (D-TREE), SVM, and KNN classifiers in system testing and 96.33% accuracy in white blood cell detection. We utilized 108 and 260 photos from the ALL-IDB-1 and ALL-IDB-2 datasets, 366 normal blood images, and 100 AML blood images from Kaggle databases. As we know, thousands of people worldwide die due to this deadly disease each year. We can reduce these deaths through early-stage detection and treatment that requires advanced technology systems.

articleTitle: Grid, Solar-Wind Bidirectional Charging System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Given the inherent unpredictability of renewable energy sources such as solar and wind, energy storage becomes essential. Battery energy storage systems, particularly lithiumion batteries due to their lightweight and high energy density, are vital for managing this intermittency. The primary objective of this research is to develop bidirectional power flow regulation between lithium-ion batteries and the single-phase grid. By connecting the grid and PV array in parallel, the EV battery can receive continuous power generation. When utilized as energy storage devices in microgrids, electric vehicle (EV) batteries can store excess energy (Grid-to-Vehicle) and return it to the grid (Vehicle-toGrid), aiding in microgrid energy management. EV charging configuration that integrates renewable energy sources enhances reliability and energy efficiency. Smart grid technologies are crucial for managing energy flow, optimizing charging schedules, and ensuring system reliability. Beyond environmental benefits, this approach fosters technical innovation and economic growth. It signifies a paradigm shift towards a more sustainable and decentralized energy landscape, leading to increased investments in renewable energy infrastructure and electric mobility. This innovative technique addresses the growing demand for sustainable energy solutions and the global adoption of electric vehicles. Through the use of renewable energy sources like solar and wind power, the concept seeks to lower carbon emissions and the reliance on fossil fuels for transportation. The bidirectional charging function enables EVs to both draw and supply power. In summary, A significant step toward a cleaner and more sustainable energy future is the grid-powered bidirectional EV charging system driven by solar and wind energy. Implementing it could lower greenhouse gas emissions, encourage the use of renewable energy sources, and strengthen the power system's resilience.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective and Low-Latency Computer Vision-Based Collision Avoidance with Remote Monitoring and Intervention
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Collision prevention through avoiding obstacles is crucial for autonomous navigation. Many works have been done to improve the techniques for detecting obstacles and facilitate autonomous navigation. However, the techniques are either very complex, requiring high computational power, or are very environment-specific. The cameras used for these techniques are also expensive. This study proposes two alternative designs that are cost-effective, low-latency, and not environment-specific. The first design uses an ultrasonic sensor, a servo motor for navigation, and ESP32 camera for remote monitoring. The second design proposes a novel methodology for detecting obstacles using Canny Edge Detection. The methodology employs tilting the camera by a certain angle to cover any range desired. It also allows the use of low-cost cameras, such as ESP32 camera, to effectively detect and avoid obstacles. The design has provisions for both remote monitoring and intervention. Rigorous tests have been conducted to determine the designs’ success rates and latency. The results show great promise as the success rate for the second design is found to be 90% while the latency found for the first design is 80 ms.

articleTitle: Utilizing Deep Learning for Detecting Malaria in Blood Cell Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Plasmodium malaria, a disease transmitted by mosquitoes, has claimed the lives of more than 7.6 million individuals. The conventional methods for detecting this disease are laborious and pose diagnostic challenges. In this study, the performance of a convolutional neural network (CNN) employing transfer learning, specifically a CNN called ShuffleNet, was investigated for classifying infected and uninfected malaria parasite cells in thick blood smears. The dataset utilized in this research comprises 26,161 images categorized into infected and uninfected cells. In this study, the dataset comprises 26,161 images categorized into infected and uninfected cells, providing a comprehensive basis for analysis. The proposed method achieved remarkable results, with a training accuracy of 99.57% and a testing accuracy of 99.77%, indicating its strong performance across various datasets. These findings underscore the potential of deep learning approaches in enhancing malaria detection from blood cell images, offering promising avenues for further research and application in clinical settings.

articleTitle: Classification and Featurization of Motherboard Components Using YOLO Through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The role of technology is vital and can be observed through the 5th industrial revolution. As a matter of fact, the impact is so severe, it can be felt almost everywhere. As technology advances, one of the most promising frontiers lies in the realm of Artificial Intelligence (AI), with machine learning at its forefront. Object detection is a crucial such part with applications in robotics and image analysis. This paper presents a comprehensive study on vision AI, focusing on the detection of motherboard components utilizing the YOLOv8 object detection framework. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and real time effectiveness of YOLOv8 in terms of motherboard object detection. Simultaneously, this work validates the feasibility of employing YOLOv8 for in-depth analysis and object detection on various circuit boards. This will allow many automated devices to repair circuit boards with the help of artificial intelligence. Consequently, allowing robots to detect flaws and repair integrated hardware components in situations considered difficult for humans.

articleTitle: Development and Evaluating a Multi-class Corpus for Recognition of Bangla Handwriting Characters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Precise recognition of Bangla handwritten characters is crucial for applications like document processing and intelligent tutoring systems. This paper presents the development and evaluation of a multi-class corpus designed for Bangla handwriting character recognition (BHCR). We describe the data collection process, addressing factors like writer demographics, character variations, and image quality. The corpus encompasses various characters, including isolated letters, conjuncts, and numerals. The corpus quality is evaluated using standard metrics for character recognition tasks. We present inter and intra-class variability analyses to assess the complexity of the corpus and its suitability for training robust systems. This research contributes a valuable dataset to the Bangla language processing community, addressing the low-resource challenges typically associated with Bangla handwriting recognition. By providing a detailed analysis of the corpus’s development and its impact on recognition accuracy, this study lays the groundwork for future advancements in the field, aiming to facilitate more e cient and accurate processing of handwritten Bangla texts. This work contributes a valuable resource for developing and evaluating BHCR systems, paving the way for improved performance and wider adoption of these technologies.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Feature Fusion with Fuzziness based Semi-Supervised Learning for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease is a prominent kind of dementia that is caused by a slow decline of cognitive abilities, including memory loss, impaired speech and diminished reactivity. The condition primarily affects brain regions responsible for cognition, memory and language and typically becomes apparent after the age of 60, with a greater risk among older individuals. To meet the requirement for early identification, researchers have explored various machine-learning techniques. To enhance the accuracy of diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease, researchers have employed supervised and unsupervised learning approaches derived from machine learning. While supervised learning relies on labelled data, obtaining sufficient labelled samples can be time-consuming and requires specialized assistance. The focus is on multiclass classification, harnessing MRI and PET data. SGLDM and SIFT feature extraction algorithms are utilized to enable the fusion of features from diverse perspectives, resulting in a robust classification model. This research introduces a novel strategy for AD diagnosis, combining multimodal feature fusion with a fuzziness-based-semi-supervised learning method. The method leverages both labeled and mislabeled data to enhance the model’s reliability. The proposed method demonstrated notable enhancements in the classifier’s performance compared to existing approaches on the dataset.

articleTitle: Exchange Rate Forecasting via Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Forecasting is an exciting topic in every field of study. Currency exchange rate Forecasting is a typical time series prediction problem which has been solved by different time-series models. Deep learning has been widely used in time series forecasting. Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) has proved to be a powerful machine learning tool in image data analysis and generation. In this paper, we propose to use Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) to learn and simulate Currency exchange rate Forecasting. More specifically, in this study, we attempt to forecast the dynamic evolutions of the exchange rates of Japanese Yen against the US dollar (JPYUSD), by using Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) & Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Networks (WGAN)

articleTitle: An Advance Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Machine Breakdown in The Steel Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The steel industry is one of the business sectors in developing countries that is expanding at a rapid rate because of its essential role in building the physical infrastructure of a country. Therefore, managing the supply chain risks of the steel industry is crucial for maintaining disruption free production. Machine breakdown and malfunction in a production line significant ones that take place in the steel industry's supply chain which could negatively impact the supplier-customer relationship. Rolling mill machines are one of the most crucial and often used machines in the steel manufacturing process. In this study, a framework has been developed to predict the machine breakdown of rolling mill machines using several advanced machine learning algorithms such as Catboost, XGboost, and LightGBM. To investigate the effectiveness of proposed approach the 'Binary Classification of Machine Failures' dataset has been used. The suggested work's effectiveness has been assessed thoroughly using proper evaluation matrices. The results indicate that CatBoost and LightGBM algorithms has achieved the best performance among all other algorithms, gaining accuracy of 99% and 97%, respectively. The proposed machine learning framework offers significant potential to enhance supply chain management in the steel industry by continuously updating machine breakdown mitigation strategies.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Techniques for Local Spinach Variant and Freshness Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Capturing the fundamental qualities and properties of the local spinach variation entails doing a thorough investigation. Examining the spinach variant's unique morphology, nutritional makeup, flavor character, and growing environment is part of this procedure. A thorough comprehension of the variant's unique characteristics is attained, making it easier to identify and distinguish it from other spinach variations. DL algorithms may be utilized to determine the freshness of the local spinach variation. One kind of DL model is the convolutional neural network (CNN), which may be educated on datasets including pictures of spinach at various stages of freshness. These models are trained to extract pertinent characteristics, including color, texture, and leaf shape, that are indicative of freshness. After training, the model can quickly and non-destructively evaluate spinach samples by correctly classifying them according to their freshness status. Using deep learning to detect freshness in the local spinach variety, an extensive framework for quality assurance and evaluation is created. This method guarantees that customers obtain a high-quality product by making it easier to identify and characterize the spinach variation and to assess its freshness in real time.

articleTitle: Crop Yields Prediction in Bangladesh: A Hybrid Machine Learning and DNN Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In todays world, machine learning and artificial intelligence are gaining popularity. In today’s digital age, many tasks are being transformed through artificial intelligence and machine learning. Agriculture, as a vital component of human sustenance, remains The principal source of livelihood for many. Bangladesh is an agrarian economy due to its geographical location. Bangladeshs economy is heavily dependent on agriculture as it contributes a lot to the countrys GDP. Even though artificial intelligence and machine learning are being used to digitize every industry in this day and age, the agricultural sector is falling behind. In Bangladesh agricultural work is mostly done in old ways and manually. From crop selection to fertilizer selection, all work is done by farmers manually based on their experience. In addition, agricultural institutions in Bangladesh use manual data, which is not a proper solution to accurately select crops and yield prediction. To address these problems, there is a need for modern and innovative approaches to yield prediction and crop selection. This paper demonstrates the most efficient and cost-efficient approach to predicting crop yield utilizing deep neural networks (DNN) and machine learning techniques. Artificial Neural Network and Machine Learning are considered powerful tools for modeling and prediction. The effectiveness of the algorithms that were assessed in this study are Deep Neural Network- Gradient Boosting Regressor(DNN-GBR),Support vector machine(SVR), K-Nearest Neighbors Algorithm. The goal of this algorithm is to improve output and prediction. The performance of the proposed hybrid DNN-GBR model was evaluated using MSE and R-squared (coefficient of determination) metrics. In this paper, we have suggested using the hybrid DNN-GBR model for agricultural yield prediction and crop selection.

articleTitle: Smart Street Lighting for Sustainable Urban Environments: Sensor-Based Automation and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In recent times, many streetlights have been wasting energy by staying on unnecessarily during the evenings and nights. This not only harms the environment but also costs a lot of money. The goal of Smart Street Lighting is to stop this wasteful energy use and make better use of resources. While other researchers have worked on this issue, we have a specific aim: to create a smart street lighting system that only turns on when it’s needed and turns off when it’s not. To achieve this, we’re using laser sensors, ZigBee wireless technology, and a powerful microprocessor. Our system identifies when there are vehicles on the road using sensors. It then turns on the streetlights only where they are needed. This saves energy by not lighting empty areas. We can control and monitor each streetlight remotely through ZigBee technology, and everything is connected to a computer that makes the streetlights work smarter. Our sensors are good at detecting objects and people with an accuracy of 89.87 percent. This innovation can reduce electricity consumption by 38.1 percent and cut lighting maintenance costs by 48 percent.

articleTitle: Unveiling Microorganism Diversity through Neural Network-driven Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Our planet has a vast diversity of microorganisms. To better understand these numerous, frequently tiny life forms, this study addresses an automated solution for microorganism classification. The motivation lies in the limitations of traditional classification methods, such as microscopy, which are time-consuming and may lack accuracy due to the abundant types of microorganisms. Therefore, whether deep learning, can provide a more effective answer for microorganism classification is the primary focus of this study. This research uses the EMDS-6 dataset, we applied preprocessing techniques, including data augmentation and image normalization, to enhance dataset quality. Our results are promising, with the proposed CNN-based model Inception v3 achieving a remarkable testing accuracy rate of 93%, signifying the potential of deep learning to significantly enhance microorganism classification. This research bridges modern deep-learning technology with biological sciences, offering valuable applications in areas like environmental monitoring, disease detection, and pharmaceutical research.

articleTitle: Securing Critical Infrastructure: A Robust DNP3 Intrusion Detection System Employing Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This study explores how different types of attacks are related to various protocols used in industrial control systems (ICSs). A study revealed that timestamps indicating when data are created, shared, modified, or deleted play a crucial role in analysing attack patterns. The focus of this empirical study is on the DNP3 protocol, which facilitates remote communication between the Systems for supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) along with industrial control System (ICS). Research incorporates a secondary dataset associated with DNP3 attacks are provided by the University of Western Macedonia. The study excluded outlier data from the analysis and used a dataset with labelled information about attack types. To enhance the results, the dataset is split into a training set (67%), a test set (22%) and a validation set (11%). By combining a randomforest classifier with the proposed model(LSTM-CNN), the study achieved an impressive accuracy of 98.3%. Research findings suggest that this model could be useful in scenarios where a cyber-attacker intercepts and discards communications between a DNP3 superintendent and a DNP3 captive device. This study introduces a novel solution by modifying the link protocol data unit DNP3 to ensure data integrity and authenticate the data origin via a recurrent neural network paired with a classification algorithm.

articleTitle: Advancing Water Quality Assessment: Leveraging XGBoost for Precise Predictive Modeling; A Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Water is the most crucial element for living organism. It is also important to maintain the quality of water. It’s crucial to ensure safety and sustainability of freshwater resources. This research focuses on assessing nine key criteria— pH, hardness, solids, chloramines, sulfate, conductivity, organic carbon, trihalomethanes, and turbidity to ensure the freshness and safety of water resources. To make this, we use various machine learning algorithms including XGBoost, random forest, logistics regression, ensemble methods etc. to make our prediction accurate. Our xgboost model achieve high accuracy of 92.5 percent for identify quality of water. The methodology involved preprocessing the dataset, performing feature engineering, hyperparameter tuning, developing machine learning models, and evaluating their performance. This study contributes to advancing water quality assessment methodologies by using the capabilities of machine learning techniques, particularly XGBoost, to enhance predictive accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Investigation Emotion Dynamics in Bangla Social Media Text for Improved Emotion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Recognizing emotion from text is fundamental to machine learning and influences our understanding of human interaction. While English sentiment analysis has been well-researched, Bengali (Bangla) is still under-researched. Our study bridges this gap by investigating the emotional dynamics in Bengali social media posts using extensive user-generated content. We use a modified dataset defined by seven emotions: Happy, Surprise, Fearful, Angry, Neutral, Disgust, and Sad. Using machine learning techniques such as support vector classifiers, decision trees, logistic regression, and random forest, we found that the Random Forest model achieved the highest accuracy of 84%. This study advances our understanding of Bengali emotional expression and demonstrates its application in social media sentiment analysis, psychoanalysis, and communication technologies. By addressing the complexities of Bengali language and culture, our work contributes to a broader definition of emotion and lays the foundation for future research in different contexts.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis and Prediction of Machine Learning Algorithms for MRI-Based Alzheimer’s Detection Using Multi-modal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In this research, various machine learning techniques were used to assess Alzheimer’s disease detection based on eleven significant criteria. The methodology included comprehensive data preprocessing, analysis, and visualization. Initial steps involved removing duplicates, handling missing values using a simple imputer with a mode strategy, and ensuring all features were appropriately scaled and encoded. Data visualization techniques, such as histograms and density plots, were used to understand the dataset’s distribution and identify outliers. We developed predictive models using supervised learning algorithms, including Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, CatBoost, SVM, KNN, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Voting Classifier. Hyperparameter tuning and grid search cross-validation were applied to enhance model performance. The Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, and CatBoost classifiers achieved the highest accuracy of 96.30 percent, followed closely by the Voting Classifier with an accuracy of 96.29 percent. KNN and Decision Tree models also showed strong performance with accuracy of 95.06 percent and 93.83 percent, respectively. SVM and Logistic Regression had lower accuracy of 92.59 percent and 90.12 percent. Visual analysis indicated that individuals aged 70-80 were more affected by Alzheimer’s disease. The study concluded that machine learning algorithms, particularly ensemble methods, are highly effective for classifying Alzheimer’s disease, providing a robust approach to understanding and predicting the disease. The findings highlight the potential of machine learning in advancing health and disease diagnostics.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Strategic Business Intelligence: A Short Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Integrating machine learning (ML) with business intelligence (BI) systems marks a significant advancement in data analysis and decision-making, allowing for more dynamic, data-driven insights and strategies. This paper explores the applications, limitations, and future directions of applying ML in business contexts, aiming to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and competitiveness. By leveraging cutting-edge ML techniques such as predictive analytics, natural language processing (NLP), and automated decision-making, businesses can gain deeper insights and make more informed decisions. This discussion encompasses various ML applications in BI, including sales forecasting, customer feedback analysis, and financial anomaly detection, highlighting their potential to optimize different aspects of business operations. The paper also addresses the challenges of integrating ML into BI, such as data quality, computational resource requirements, and model interpretability, along with ethical and privacy concerns. By examining the latest research and practical implementations, this paper aims to provide a comprehensive roadmap for leveraging ML in business intelligence, ultimately driving innovation and growth in the modern business landscape.

articleTitle: Identification of Key Signaling Pathways and Novel Computational Drug Target for Depression and Coronary Artery Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Psychological disorders, such as anxiety, bipolar disorder, panic disorder, stress, depression, and schizophrenia, are increasingly prevalent worldwide. Among these conditions, depression is particularly notable as one of the most common and debilitating neuropsychiatric disorders. Individuals with depression may be at a higher risk of developing oronary Artery Disease (CAD). Depression can contribute to poor lifestyle choices, such as unhealthy eating, lack of exercise, and smoking, which are risk factors for CAD. The emotional stress and anxiety associated with depression can strain the heart and exacerbate CAD symptoms. The relationship is not one-sided. CAD itself can be a significant source of emotional distress, leading to symptoms of depression and anxiety in affected individuals. Managing both conditions in tandem can be complicated. Treating CAD may involve medications, lifestyle modifications, and potentially surgical interventions. Meanwhile, depression often requires therapy, counseling, and medication. Coordinating care and addressing both conditions simultaneously is crucial. In our study, we investigated the molecular connections between CAD and Depression using GSE98793 and GSE20681 microarray datasets. After preprocessing, we identified key hub genes, including CCT2, SVIL, REPS2, ASPH, and UBC, in the shared ProteinProtein Interaction network. KEGG pathways linked these DEGs to colorectal and cancer pathways. Our next steps involve exploring microRNAs, TFs, and GO analysis. These findings offer promising leads for potential therapies, uniting CAD and Depression under a common molecular framework, advancing our understanding of these conditions.

articleTitle: Cricket Analytics: ODI Match Score Prediction and Resource Metric Modeling using Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Sports analytics using machine learning is no longer a young area of computer science research that presents several difficulties. The purpose of this study is to develop a method for predicting game outcomes during an ODI cricket competition. Like all other papers, we adopted the factor-based prediction meaning the prediction will depend on various game factors like wickets left, overs left, current run, run rate, etc. Sometimes the models can not make good predictions based on these factors and we tried to improve that by adding weight to overs and wickets because these two vastly control the score of the game. We named this feature the resource factor. We used linear regression, polynomial regression, elastic net regression, Xgboost, and random forest and found that random forest works best for our dataset. For more interaction, we used a web application and we applied our best model to predict the score. For the test phase, the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score for the random forest regressor is 0.9899 which is pretty good, and for the MAE and MSE scores, we have got 3.3569 and 37.3555.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Pupil Size Changes for Lie Detection in a Biofeedback Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Recognizing a person’s intention has always been a part of psychological research. The current study investigates the potential of detecting false statements based on changes in pupil size. In two controlled laboratory experiments we differentiate pupil responses to intentional lies and to false statements made at the request of others. In addition, we use real-time feedback on pupil diameter to investigate the potential for voluntary suppression of dilation in the context of a false claim. The results show larger pupil diameters during free choices compared to instructed statements, especially when comparing the individual decision to lie to being asked to tell the truth. However, real-time feedback did not support voluntary control of pupil size changes.

articleTitle: White Blood Cells to Classify Leukemic Blood Images Using Deep Learning and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: White Blood Cell (WBC) count is a significant task in identifying leukemia, a widely known malignancy that can be devastating gradually. Infantile WBCs existing in the sponge tissues of bone marrow affect the superfluous expansion, which in turn produces leukemia cancer. Deep learning and image processing techniques models can be applied in the field to detect leukemic blood and generate outstanding outcomes. Leukemia occurs from the leukocyte blood type, which is one kind of white blood cell. This proposed system introduces a method of classifying leukemic blood images and counting the number of white blood cells in a Leukemic blood image. This is a hybrid procedure combining deep learning and image processing techniques. A collection of 221 blood cell images available on a website known as ‘RaabinData’ is used, which were collected from patients at the Takht-e Tavoos Medical School Laboratory in Tehran. Using this dataset, this study achieves 96.74% accuracy in counting white blood cells.

articleTitle: LeukoDeepNet: A Novel Approach in Automated Identification of Leukemia Diseases in Microscopic Human Blood Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Leukemia, a critical hematologic malignancy, demands early and accurate diagnosis for effective treatment. In this research, we present a comprehensive approach to the detection of leukemia based on microscopic human blood cell images. Our research is dedicated to the early detection of leukemia by leveraging deep learning techniques on microscopic blood cell images. The study introduces a new modified VGG16 model, LeukoDeepNet, and compares it with conventional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Inception (GoogLeNet) models. LeukoDeepNet stands out with remarkable training and validation accuracies of 99.96% and 92.63%, along with low training and validation losses of 0.0013 and 0.6295, respectively. These findings underscore the success of the approach and its potential to enhance both leukemia diagnosis and treatment.

articleTitle: Automated Convict Identification Through Machine Learning-Based Facial Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In a world riddled with criminal incidents, the swift identification of wrongdoers remains an ongoing challenge. Criminals have become adept at erasing biological and fingerprint traces from crime scenes, rendering traditional investigative methods ineffective. Modern facial identification technologies offer a rapid solution to this problem. With the widespread use of CCTV cameras, driven by security technology advancements, a unique opportunity arises. Our research seeks to automatically detect and identify convicts from video footage, providing a powerful tool for law enforcement. This technology extends to identifying suspects, criminals, missing persons, and more, saving valuable time and effort. Our study focuses on developing a machine learning-based criminal face detection system to streamline law enforcement by automating criminal identification. Employing a mixed methods approach involving data collection and focus group discussions, we gain insights from field practitioners. Our survey reveals a significant challenge in identifying culprits, with nearly 60% of cases analyzed yielding unidentified perpetrators. We propose a novel machine learning based automated method, which integrates with a comprehensive database containing individuals’ information and diverse images. Once identified, the system conducts real-time database comparisons, providing immediate results when a match is found. We explore techniques for criminal identification from photographs and introduce innovative ideas. Our research comprehensively covers various models, offering a promising solution to the challenges of locating and identifying convicts in modern law enforcement.

articleTitle: Advancing Multi-Class Arc Welding Defect Classification: DEEPTLWELD Intelligent System Utilizing Computer Vision, Deep Learning, and Transfer Learning on Radiographic X-ray Images for Bangladesh's Manufacturing Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Welding defects are a crucial problem in the manufacturing industry. However, the industry faces enormous losses for these defects. Conditional monitoring and quality control can reduce this loss. In Industry 4.0, artificial intelligence revolutionized every field. This research aims to improve industrial automation by creating a multi-class classification system through digital image processing, deep learning, and transfer learning—a real-time application integrated with deep learning, transfer learning, image processing, and MLOPS operations. Accurate prediction occurred by various models, such as custom CNN and pre-trained models (InceptionV3, EfficientNetB7, DenseNet201, and ResNet152). DEEPTLWELD system was developed using a bespoke dataset of 4,000 radiographic X-ray pictures with four frequent categories of defects that are essential for tackling difficulties faced by local industry challenges. This dataset is All radiographic images processed with image processing techniques (distance transform, watershed transform, edge detection). In the transfer learning part, weights were loaded manually as those weights performed better with a particular model. Out of the networks, custom CNN achieved high accuracy with 98% after fine-tuning. The deployment of the produced model in a production environment developed with a Streamlit framework is ensured by its smooth integration into a machine learning pipeline housed on Amazon EC2 servers. This intelligent system has the potential for broader applications in inclusive technology.

articleTitle: Hypothyroid Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning & Ensemble Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Thyroid illness is spreading more and more nowadays and it has become the most common disease that can lead to various health disorders. The main reason behind this disease is thyroid hormone disorder which can lead to problems like Hypothyroidism or Hyperthyroidism. As the problem is often underestimated, it is necessary but challenging to predict it efficiently. To diagnose Hypothyroidism, the traditional way is to perform thyroid tests based on various elements to diagnose the behavior of thyroid hormone. Machine learning algorithms play an important in detecting and predicting diseases at their early stages. Many analyses and models can be developed using machine learning classifiers to find the most effective and accurate predictions. Our study aims to use different machine-learning classification techniques and develop a model to predict hypothyroidism. We also compare machine learning methods to determine which classifier is optimal for constructing a classification model. We also aim to use ensemble learning techniques for optimal results and amplify accuracies. We have achieved 97.23% with gradient boosting and the AdaBoost classifier and gradient boosting are the best-performing models combined with the Boosting method giving the highest accuracy of 97.57% and 97.51% respectively.

articleTitle: Classifying CCTV Image for Road Accident Analysis Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Accident detection plays a pivotal role in enhancing road safety and minimizing the impact of unforeseen events. This research addresses the challenge through the lens of deep learning, employing a comprehensive analysis of four state-of-the-art convolutional neural network models— ResNet50, VGG-19, DenseNet201 and Ensemble Model (EfficientMobileNet). In this work, we develop a robust multiclass accident detection system capable of accurately classifying diverse accident scenarios from visual data. The experiments reveal distinct performance characteristics, shedding light on the strengths and weaknesses of the individual architectures. In our work we collect almost 4800 images data which is collected from various sources like traffic monitoring systems, surveillance cameras, CCTV footage and videos. Dataset contains four classes (bike, bus, car, non-accident) and after training all pre-trained models among them DenseNet-201 outperforms others with the accuracy of 98.24%. This study contributes to the ongoing discourse on leveraging deep CNNs for safety-critical applications, offering valuable insights for researchers and practitioners alike.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of a PCF-Based SPR Sensor Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: A unique Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF)-based Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) sensor design using a Machine Learning Inverse approach has been proposed in this work. The sensor is designed to predict the input parameters required to achieve a desired output. The inverse design method for the PCF-based SPR sensor streamlines the design process by predicting optimal parameters and reducing trial-and-error iterations. It also enables exploring a wider parameter space, leading to innovative sensor designs, with predictions falling within a ±10% error range around the zero line, indicating high accuracy. This approach minimizes computation time and resources, eliminating the need for extensive simulations, and makes the sensor a cost-effective, time-saving, and highly adaptable alternative for various sensing applications.

articleTitle: Using ImageNet Xception Model to Identify Skin Cancer and Non-Skin Cancer Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Skin cancer is a significant public health concern, requiring efficient and accurate diagnostic tools. This research explores the application of deep learning, specifically the Xception architecture, for bi- nary classification using images of skin cancer and non-skin cancer conditions. Two datasets, comprising 250 training images and 40 testing images, were Selection carefully and augmented to enhance model generalization. The Xception model, pre-trained on ImageNet, demonstrated superior performance with a 94 percent accuracy compared to an initial convolutional neural network (CNN) model. A comprehensive analysis, including a confusion matrix and sample predictions, provides in- sights into the model’s predictive behavior. We also use SHAP values from explainable AI using Xception Model.

articleTitle: Predicting Pancreatic Cancer Survival and Staging: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Pancreatic cancer, it is known as one of the most aggressive one among cancers due to its sudden progression and hard to treat manner. The insidious characteristic of pancreatic cancer is known to be the main reason behind its being the 3rd among fatal cancers. The most common symptoms of this disease are jaundice, weight loss, abdominal pain and loss of appetite. In spite of having such prominent symptoms, this disease normally does not show any of them until an advanced stage of cancer for almost 90% of patients thus making it harder to treat. The treatment targeting cure can be applied or even made faster depending on the shape and site of the eruption whether it is spread out to the whole abdomen or other part of the body or not. Focusing this issue, we implemented our work towards detection of the disease and stage specification. Our algorithm can be used to detect the place and shape of the eruption. In particular, we are to find out the stage and survivability of this disease. Keeping that in mind, we are applying various tree-based algorithms to mark the best one. The algorithms that we have put into practice are the Gaussian NB, Random Forest, Decision Tree, AdaBoost, Bagging, Extra Trees, MLP, and Quadratic Discriminant Analysis classifiers. In our study, the decision tree performs the best among these tree-based algorithms with a 92.1% accuracy in the test dataset for survivability.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Brain Stroke Prediction Using Various Pretrained CNN and ViT models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Deep Learning is a technique in which the system analyzes and learns, is one of the most common applications of artificial intelligence that has seen tremendous progress in the digital era. Because of advancements of deep learning in healthcare technology, a growing number of studies have sought to anticipate and assess certain diseases in advance. Stroke illness research is a hot topic right now, especially among the elderly. Stroke, which is lethal in the elderly, is a condition that needs constant medical attention and monitoring due to its high recurrence and fatality rates. So far, the majority of investigations into stroke disease have relied on MRI or CT imaging for straightforward categorization. The goal of this is to use deep learning to detect whether there are initial signs of a brain stroke using CT or MRI images. Using CT or MRI scan pictures, a classifier can predict brain stroke. By using four Pre–trained models such as ResNet-50, Vision Transformer (Vit), MobileNetV2 and VGG-19, we obtained our desired results. The study h ighlights the capabilities of various pretrained CNN models and provides a comparison with Vit models and attempts to discuss limitations of various architectures.

articleTitle: Computer Vision Based Waste Classification and Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Different type of garbage disposal is becoming a major issue in metropolitan areas. To dispose the garbage, land-filling is used generally which is inefficient, costly, and it pollutes the environment. In order to avoid dangerous exposure to contaminated waste, this article has proposed a computer vision-based waste classification system which will make the waste separation process quicker and more intelligent, possibly even without or with reduced human participation. The proposed system collects waste images from a camera, performs object recognition module to detect wastes, and categorizes the detected waste materials into 8 classes (Plastic, paper, glass, metal, battery, organic, cloth, and e-wast). After classifying the wast, the system feeds the wastes into recyclable and non-recyclable bins. We have used improved VGG19 model for the system training and testing. A total of 16,830 images are used of 8 classes image maintaining 80:20 training and testing ratio achieving the accuracy 97.75% for the proposed improved VGG19 where as basic VGG19 achieves 87.40% accuracy.

articleTitle: An Encryption Approach with Steganography for Enhanced Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The present study focuses on the protection of confidential information. Steganography and cryptography are techniques used to hide secret information within files and make it unreadable to unauthorised individuals. The current approach employs a hashing method to protect the less secure element, namely the Advanced Encryption Standard key. The suggested approach enhances the level of information secrecy and covert information exchange by encrypting the data and embedding it within a multimedia file, specifically an image. A cipher text is generated through the encryption of a text using the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), a highly secure encryption technique that has been in use for a considerable duration. This encryption process employs a 256-bit hash key generated by the Secure Hash Algorithm 256. By employing the Discrete Wavelet Transform, the encrypted text is seamlessly embedded into the target image, modifying it in a manner that remains imperceptible to human vision. It ensures that the aesthetic integrity of an image is maintained. Human eyes occasionally perceive the distortion or modification in the picture. The system’s performance is assessed using statistical measures, namely peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), mean square error (MSE), and structural similarity (SSIM).The PSNR values indicate superior image quality, while the low Mean Squared Error (MSE) values suggest that the model performs well with low variance and an appropriate fit. Additionally, the SSIM values signify excellent quality, minimal degradation, and effective compression or enhancement. The proposed model has shown its capability to send a cover picture with high invisibility, minimal deterioration in the received stego-image, and the capacity to hide confidential information.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Pumpkin Leaf Diseases Using Transfer Learning and a Custom Dataset from Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Pumpkin plays a significant role in Bangladeshi agriculture, serving as both a vital food source and a component of the local economy. In this work, we have created a new dataset of pumpkin leaves and trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models for pumpkin leaf disease detection. The dataset contains 4000 images, illustrating various pumpkin diseases including Downy Mildew, Powdery Mildew, Mosaic Disease, Bacterial Leaf Spot, and images of healthy leaves. We trained four CNN models on this dataset—EfficientNet, MobileNet, DenseNet, and ResNet50—to categorize the pumpkin leaf diseases. Data augmentations were implemented to improve the strength of the models. The accuracy of ResNet50, EfficientNet, MobileNet, and DenseNet for classifying pumpkin leaf diseases was found to be 74.68%, 79.74%, 95.44%, and 97.82%, respectively, with DenseNet demonstrating superior accuracy. By identifying the most efficacious model, this research contributes to the advancement of efficient and adaptable solutions for plant disease diagnosis, ultimately aiming to enhance crop management and productivity in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Using Deep Learning to Analyze Brain fMRI for Schizophrenia Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in diagnosing schizophrenia patients through functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) data, as early detection of schizophrenia, is crucial for symptom management. The study evaluates the performance of five state-of-the-art CNN models (VGG16, Resnet50, Inception V3, Inception Resnet V2, EfficientNetB0) in conjunction with a custom CNN model for binary classification. By utilizing a dataset of 19,734 fMRI images, an effective approach for classifying schizophrenia patients and healthy controls with remarkable accuracy has been introduced. These approaches involve model modification, image pre-processing techniques, and hyperparameter tuning. Notably, grayscale conversion, binary thresholding, and 3-channel format conversion contribute significantly to enhanced classification accuracy. The incorporation of data augmentation and layer modification schemes further strengthens the methodology. Moreover, through meticulous layer modifications, the layer-modified VGG16 and the customized CNN model achieved more than 99.99%, while other models reached an accuracy of 99.9%.

articleTitle: Leveraging Transfer Learning for Accurate Detection of Diseases in Rice Leaf Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: A food source for billions of people worldwide, particularly in East and Southeast Asia, is rice. Unfortunately, several diseases, including bacterial blight, blast, brown spot, and tungro, can seriously reduce yields and often compromise the crop's ability to produce it. Using a dataset of 5,932 in-field images, this study explores the application of transfer learning to precisely identify and categorize these common rice leaf diseases. While pesticides may increase crop yields, they often degrade rice quality, which emphasizes the importance of early and accurate illness detection identification in order to assist farmers in minimizing losses. Using the most recent innovations in deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN), this study assesses the classification performance of five cutting-edge models: Xception, DenseNet121, InceptionResNetV2, ResNet50V2, and EfficientNetB0. The images underwent extensive pre-processing and data augmentation to enhance the quality and Variation of the training set, thereby improving model efficiency and generalization. With a 99.99% accuracy rate on the Mendeley dataset, the Xception model outperformed the other tested models. The results underscore the potential of transfer learning in agricultural disease diagnosis, offering a powerful tool for farmers to implement timely interventions and protect their crops from devastating losses.

articleTitle: Dermatological Disease Detection Using Image Processing and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Skin Disease is now spreading at an alarming rate. People are not aware of different types of skin diseases and for lack of treatment, it is spreading from people to people. In this study, we have tried to make skin disease detection and identification easy and simple with three different convolutional neural network architectures, namely U-Net, VGG19, and MobileNetV2, for the task of skin disease classification. Our objective is to identify the most suitable model that achieves superior accuracy in distinguishing between 7 different types of skin conditions. We have conducted experiments on a skin disease image dataset with corresponding masks. The data was preprocessed and augmented, ensuring good model training. Each architecture went under rigorous training and evaluation, with a focus on achieving high accuracy in disease classification. From our findings U-Net model emerged as the most effective, achieving an impressive accuracy of 93% on the test set.

articleTitle: An Investigative Approach to Knee Osteoarthritis Detection Using Deep Learning on X-ray Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: A chronic joint condition called osteoarthritis affects the ligaments, capsule, synovium, subchondral bone, and articular cartilage. Osteoarthritis most frequently develops in the knee joints. A scoring system developed by Kellgren and Lawrence (KL) is used to measure the severity of osteoarthritis. The range of the KL score is 0–4. Grades 0 through 4 represent normal, doubtful mild, moderate, and severe, respectively. In this work, we classified 3 levels of Osteoarthritis by modifying the KL scoring system. This research identifies grade 0 for normal and doubtful, grade 1 for mild and moderate, and grade 2 for severe. To identify these classes from knee radiograph images, we used a deep-learning architecture namely ResNet-50, and customized it. Using our proposed model, we achieved 97% training accuracy. Clinical researchers will find this research useful in effectively determining the degree of osteoarthritis in the knee.

articleTitle: Eye Disease Detection And Classification Using Deep Learning: A Comperative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Eye disease detection is a critical task in medical diagnostics, particularly for conditions that can lead to vision impairment or blindness if left untreated. Recent advancements in deep learning have demonstrated promise in enhancing accuracy and efficiency of medical image analysis. This research focuses on the development and evaluation of deep learning-based model for detecting various eye diseases using retinal images. The proposed model leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to automatically extract property from retinal images and classify them into categories such as diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration, and cataracts. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed deep learning model gains high accuracy, sensitivity and specificity in finding out eye disease from retinal images. We achieved an impressive 100% training accuracy, along with strong 94% validation and testing accuracy. We suffered relatively little loss. Additionally, we attained 100% recall, f1-score, and precision, demonstrating high performance. Comparative analysis with traditional image processing methods highlights the superiority of deep learning approaches in terms of both performance and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Machine Learning-Based Method to Determine the Presence of Heart Ailment Using Pooled Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Heart disease remains the leading cause of mortality globally, emphasizing the critical need for better diagnostics. This study used a variety of machine learning methods to forecast cardiac disease, using SVM, Random Forest, Decision Tree, KNN, and LGBM. The evaluation measures include accuracy, ROC, precision, recall, and F1 score. Data pretreatment procedures such as cleansing, transformation, integration, and reduction were used to guarantee reliable analysis. The model's performance was further enhanced by hyperparameter tuning. SVM had the lowest performance of the models examined, with 57.23% accuracy, 86% precision, 89% recall, and an F1 score of 87%. The study used three different datasets, combining their strengths to improve model discrimination, decrease overfitting, and increase overall accuracy. We developed multiple models from the combination of RF, DT and LGBM. We found accuracy of up to 99.54% by merging LGBM and Random Forest. These findings illustrate the efficacy of the ensemble approaches and data integration in improving heart disease prediction skills using machine learning.

articleTitle: Transformer Based Bangla-English Code-Switching Speech Recognition and Language Identification Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The growing ubiquity of bilingual and multilingual communication presents serious difficulties for conventional Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system in the field of voice recognition. Code-switching is a major problem for traditional ASR systems because it enables two or more languages to be switched into one conversation. In this paper, the model can detect the language (whether Bangla or English) from a spoken sentence and also perform the ASR task from this mixed voice. For this context, XLSR Wav2vec 2.0 encoder has been used for feature extraction, CTC (Connectionist Temporal Classification) is used for ASR purpose and LID (Language Identification) for language identification task. By applying this approach, it is found that the Word Error Rate (WER) is 21.5% and the Language Identification (LID) accuracy is 70%. The suggested approach shows notable gains over any other models and provides a viable method for precise and effective ASR and LID in code switching.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Customized ACL-Net Model: A Comparative Analysis of CNN and Image Enhancement Techniques for Classifying ACL Injuries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays a crucial role in diagnosing knee injuries and joint conditions, particularly in detecting anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) damage that can impact knee stability. This research employed various convolutional neural network (CNN) models, including the customized ACL-Net, to classify ACL conditions in MRI image datasets, applying image processing techniques for dataset enhancement. ACL-Net outperformed, achieving 93.75%, 91.56%, 87.44%, and 90.65% accuracy for full-sized, enhanced, ROI-cropped, and ROI-cropped enhanced MRI images, respectively. The findings suggest that ACL-Net is a promising tool for automated knee ligament injury classification in MRI images, with clinical diagnostic potential.

articleTitle: A YOLO-Based Framework for Road Sign Detection and Recognition in the Context of Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Road accidents pose a significant global threat, exacerbated by diverse road conditions and inadequate traffic management systems in Bangladesh. This research addresses these issues by improving traffic sign detection and identification technology, which is critical for ITS and ADAS. This work emphasizes the critical role of accurate road sign identification in improving roadway security and traffic management, and it makes use of advanced models, namely the YOLO models. A major contribution of this work is the development of the Bangladeshi Road Sign Detection Dataset (BRSDD), comprising 9,133 annotated images spanning 29 distinct classes of Bangladeshi road signs. This dataset fills a critical gap, providing a comprehensive resource to train and evaluate detection models tailored specifically to Bangladesh. Evaluation of the YOLOv8 model on the BRSDD demonstrates significant performance with a precision of 0.986, with a recall of 0.999, surpassing earlier versions, YOLOv5 and YOLOv7, in mean average precision. Integrating YOLOv8 with ADAS enhances real-time road sign recognition, supporting improved road safety and traffic management practices. This research lays the groundwork for integrating advanced computer vision into ITS, customized to local road conditions, to effectively advance traffic safety and management strategies.
