In conclusion, this particular research work advances road sign detection technology and offers practical solutions to enhance road safety, traffic management, and overall transportation efficiency in Bangladesh.

articleTitle: AR-TurtleSLAM: EKF-based Localization and Mapping using ArUco Feature Detection on Mobile Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Localization is fundamental for mobile robots, especially in indoor environments where GPS cannot work properly. This paper presents an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF)-based approach for simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) utilizing ArUco marker detection for mobile robots. The EKF framework integrates sensor data from the robot’s odometry for prediction and camera for update, effectively managing the uncertainties inherent in real-world environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the EKF-based SLAM system achieves reliable performance in controlled environments, maintaining precise localization and producing accurate maps. This approach offers a cost-effective and computational efficient solution for localizing mobile robots in indoor environments, with potential applications in robotics research and controlled industry scenarios.

articleTitle: A Bengali Physics Chatbot Utilizing Sequence-to-Sequence Model with Beam Search
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Chatbots, also known as talkbots or interactive agents, are software applications designed to facilitate communication between humans and machines. While most students in Bangladesh currently waste their valuable time engaging in casual conversations with each other, using a Bengali educational chatbot for such interactions would provide them with a more beneficial use of their time by providing hand note-wise answers for physics. The challenge faced by a Bengali chatbot lies in the necessity of creating a dataset in Bengali, given the scarcity of available Bengali datasets online. We have developed a physics-focused educational chatbot, akin to personalized hand notes, offering comprehensive answers to aid students in learning and revising complex physics concepts. The development of chatbots involves diverse techniques, including rule-based systems, machine learning-based approaches, and generative models. Our proposed system implements the seq2seq model with a beam search decoding algorithm, featuring BiLSTM layers for enhanced context understanding and efficient exploration of potential output sequences. This approach outperforms traditional seq2seq models, ensuring higher accuracy and delivering high-quality responses. Finally, we obtained the highest BLEU1, BLEU2, BLEU3, and BLEU4 scores, respectively, of 0.52, 0.41, 0.29, and 0.23.

articleTitle: Utilizing Deep Learning for Microscopic Image Based Bacteria Species Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Clinical microbiology receives significant advantages from automated bacterial species identification and classification using microscopic images. Bacterial classification from microscopy pictures takes a long time and is difficult even for expert biologists; thus, in this paper, an automated deep learning-based classification strategy is provided. The purpose of this work is to offer a feasibility study using polyculture images to reduce diagnostic time and expense. The ResNet50 pre-trained architecture method was utilized to divide digital images into 33 categories. ResNet50 has remarkable feature extraction abilities through precise data preprocessing and model training. Enhancing robustness augmentation techniques enables accurate classification even with unseen data. This method obtained an average classification accuracy of 94.91% and can be used for any bacterial classification. This model is ready to use in the clinical microbiology section.

articleTitle: Design a Quick Responder Smart Hairband as Safety Solution for the Women
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: At present, it is the most pressing challenges in current world to really insure about the safety of women in our society. It’s turn into a vital mission to protect them. The women’s cannot lead themselves smoothly in their dream, and their professional life due to different crimes such as harassment, assault, rape, abuse, etc. against women. Every day, almost every woman from all profession are fighting to be protected and secure themselves from people of perverted humanity who tease, onslaught and defile the honor of women regularly. To assist them, there are different devices and apps are available as a safety solution for women. But the existing solutions are not effective due to requiring a lot of human interaction. This research suppose a smart wearable hairband which will be work as a spy for the user and able to protect women. The proposed system incorporated a pulse rate sensor to monitor user heart rate for anomalies. Upon detecting irregularities, the device determined the user’s location via GPS and transmitted SMS alerts to designated contacts and the nearest police station using GSM network It’s very well known that the Facebook is the most popular social platform and everyone are steadily associate with messenger, so any type of help post or message from the victims Facebook ID are easily reachable to friends and family members through this medium. Therefore, in addition, Raspberry Pi W was employed to generate a location-based assistance post on Facebook and dispatch help messages from the user’s account to all their Facebook friends via Messenger which are the prominent features of this device. The device responded very quickly so that family members and others will detect the victim’s place, rescue her and catching the criminal immediately. In our system, Arduino Nano serves as a controller of the device. The proposed device is cost-efficient, responded quickly, user-friendly, easy to control, and consume low battery.

articleTitle: From Image to Emotion: Exploring CNN Architectures for Facial Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Facial Emotion Recognition (FER) has made significant accomplishments over the past few years while the implications of it are quite extensive and are found in different domains. In this paper, a deep learning-based architecture is proposed for FER where we mainly focus on the main components, including dataset preparation; preprocessing methods; feature extraction techniques; classification algorithm; and XAI approaches. The proposed model based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) operates with feature extraction from facial images. Preprocessing techniques such as resizing, normalization, and augmentation are used to elevate the quality and variety of the dataset. Due to the architecture of VGG16 and ResNet50, we implement three CNN models to extract discriminant features from facial expressions. Meanwhile, each model works as a classifier so that it can make accurate classifications. On the other hand, we use saliency maps to give the model the computation process in a more interpretable manner. Through multiple experimentation and evaluation, the established model shown the high accuracy of the regional analysis of facial emotions, and, as a result, FE R systems can be updated by the improved performance and explainability.

articleTitle: Exploring Transformer Models for Sentiment Analysis in Airline Service Reviews
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Given the substantial expansion of the airline sector in the last twenty years, it has become imperative to have efficient techniques for evaluating customer input in order to improve service provision. Using a variety of machine learning approaches on two separate datasets and their merged form, this research paper examines the effectiveness of sentiment analysis in extracting attitudes and emotions from airline service ratings. Initially, conventional machine learning methods including Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), AdaBoost, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Decision Trees were used. Among them, Random Forest demonstrated the best level of accuracy, reaching 99% on one of the available datasets. Following that, a hybrid model employing Convolutional Neural Networks and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-Bi-LSTM) was investigated, achieving a maximum accuracy of 98%. The research subsequently progressed to utilizing transformer-based models such as DistilBERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT, Electra, and two versions of BERT (basic and big), with a specific emphasis on their ability to effectively process intricate contextual information. Despite comparable performance metrics among models, ALBERT demonstrated a little lower accuracy of 97% in a specific dataset, highlighting the intricate capabilities of transformer structures.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of ML and DL Models for Discriminating Autistic vs Non-Autistic Spectrum Disorder Using Facial Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Autism is a developmental disorder affecting children's brains, characterized by challenges in social communication, behavior, and imagination. Globally, approximately one in a hundred children is affected by autism. Early screening and diagnosis are crucial for timely educational planning, family support, and medical intervention. This work investigates the development of prediction models for the diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in children using facial image analysis and machine learning (ML) approaches. We made use of a DATASET that included 2926 images of children's faces, both typical and autistic. Alongside a deep learning (DL) technique called the convolutional neural network (CNN), traditional machine learning (ML) approaches such as logistic regression (LR), linear discriminant analysis (LDA), support vector machines (SVM), naïve Bayes (NB), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and decision trees (DT) were used. With an F1-score of 75.10% and the best accuracy of 70.15% among the ML models, NB was the most successful. Nevertheless, the CNN model achieved an accuracy of 93.98% and an F1-score of 94.32%, outperforming conventional ML models. The selection of an appropriate model configuration is critical, and further research is needed to optimize the architecture, activation functions, and preprocessing techniques to enhance accuracy. High-accuracy models offer significant potential for aiding in the detection of autism and the development of communication and physical skills.

articleTitle: Deep Facial Recognition: Unraveling Kinship Patterns Among Strangers Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This study explores the application of deep facial recognition technology to identify kinship patterns among strangers using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Utilizing the VGGFace2 dataset, a deep CNN model was developed and evaluated to determine its effectiveness in inferring familial relationships based on facial features. The model achieved an impressive accuracy of 95%, demonstrating its potential for accurately recognizing kinship. This research highlights the promising applications of facial feature analysis in various domains, including forensic science and social network research. Additionally, it addresses both technological and ethical considerations, contributing to the responsible development and application of facial recognition technology for establishing familial ties. The comprehensive evaluation provided in this study underscores the potential and implications of facial recognition technology in determining kinship, while also identifying areas for future research and improvement.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models for Classification of Red Blood Cells in Microscopy Images for Anemia Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Anemia, a condition affecting human red blood cells (RBCs), presents in various forms. Different blood cell types and anemia variants exist. Addressing such a significant challenge requires integrating pathophysiology, advanced technology, and a comprehensive understanding of RBC classifications. In this pursuit, we utilize Deep Learning (DL) models to establish connections and propose innovative solutions to pathophysiological issues related to anaemia diagnosis through RBC classification. The customized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) demonstrates exceptional performance, boasting a Training Accuracy of 99.42% and a Test Accuracy of 98.88%. Furthermore, the Training Loss is impressively low at 0.0232, while the Validation Loss remains minimal at 0.0964. The associated confusion matrix attests to the model's robust performance, affirming its accuracy in classification tasks.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Algorithms for Emotion Detection using EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Assessment of clinical subjects’ cognitive functions and state is essential to e-healthcare delivery and developing novel human-machine interfaces. With the advancements in brain physiology research, electroencephalogram (EEG)-based emotion detection has emerged as an intriguing and popular study area. The emotion detection model can be implemented in human mental health monitoring, therapeutic support, law enforcement agencies, driver monitoring, etc. Numerous studies have been conducted in the last few decades to use EEG waves to detect emotions. In these research articles, an exhaustive study was not shown to find the best Machine Learning (ML) algorithms for multi-class emotion detection. Moreover, most of these researchers used a large number of electrodes in the experiment, which creates complexity in real-time setup. Therefore, the primary objective of this study is to identify the most effective ML algorithm that gives the expected accuracy using a single electrode. The proposed research has been done on the SEED-IV dataset to classify four common types of emotions: Happy, Fear, Sad, and Neutral. Different types of standard ML classifiers, including ensemble ML classifiers, have been used in this experiment. The performance of this study has been assessed by splitting and 10-fold cross-validation. Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) shows a better classification rate of 72.22% and 72.31% among all the classifiers according to Accuracy and F1 score. This study’s results anticipate opening up new possibilities for neuroscience by demonstrating that single-channel EEG data alone is sufficient for categorizing emotions.

articleTitle: Forest Fire Detection Using Ensemble Deep Learning Model With XAi
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The incidence of forest fires seems to be rising and causing damages to the environment and properties, as well as loss of lives. The high rate of forest fires therefore requires effective early detection systems to address the catastrophic challenges the disasters pose. Traditional methods of fire detection, which rely heavily on direct visual observation systems and conventional sensor devices, are often slow and inadequate. This study introduces an intelligent detection system that integrates Deep learning with Explainable AI (XAI) to improve the early identification of forest fires. We developed an ensemble model integrating ResNet50V2 and InceptionV3 architectures. This study uses explainer techniques from XAI like LIME and Grad-CAM to ensure that the results meet compliance and performance standards as well as to reveal possible biases and flaws in the model’s decision-making process. The findings indicate that incorporating an ensemble model significantly improves detection by achieving a high accuracy of 98%. It also showed better results regarding distinguishing between fire and no-fire conditions. Based on the approaches outlined in this paper, including XAI for model interpretability means that advanced deep learning models can be reliable and more effective even for real-world applications in forest fire detection.

articleTitle: Utilizing Machine Learning for Early Detection of Chronic Kidney Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The study employed a range of machine learning and deep learning techniques to predict Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) using clinical data containing 24 predictive parameters. CKD, characterized by abnormal kidney function or renal failure over an extended period, necessitates accurate early-stage prediction for effective management. Machine learning emerged as a robust tool for this purpose, exhibiting superior performance compared to deep learning and other methods. The methodology encompassed data preprocessing, addressing missing values, and feature extraction before applying various machine learning algorithms. These included K-nearest neighbor, Gradient Boosting, as well as deep learning models like CNN and ANN. The dataset comprised 400 individuals, with 250 diagnosed with CKD. Among the techniques evaluated, Gradient Boosting classification stood out as the most accurate, achieving a remarkable 97% accuracy in predicting Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) status. This method streamlined feature selection, enabling the identification of crucial predictors while maintaining high predictive performance.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Classifying Mental Health Features in the Tech Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Mental health has emerged as a critical topic in contemporary discourse due to its significant impact on individuals’ lives and well-being. This research aims to classify various target features related to mental health in the workplace, such as discussions about mental health between employers and employees, coworker interactions concerning mental health, the prevalence of mental health issues, the adequacy of resources provided, and the utilization of these resources. We applied several machine learning models including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Neural Network, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression, and compared their performances. The OSMI (Open Sourcing Mental Illness) survey dataset was utilized to train these models. We employed advanced techniques such as feature engineering and derived feature creation to enhance model performance. Additionally, chi-square testing was crucial in identifying significant relationships between different variables in the dataset. The accuracy of classifying features discussions about mental health between employers and employees, coworker interactions concerning mental health, the prevalence of mental health issues, the adequacy of resources provided, and the utilization of these resources are SVM 83.94%, Neural Network 93.98%, XGBoost 83.34%, SVM 83.94%, and Random Forest 85.54% respectively. This research contributes to the growing field of mental health analytics, offering a data-driven approach to identifying and addressing mental health issues in professional settings.

Author Keywords: Open Sourcing Mental Illness Survey Dataset

articleTitle: Stacking Ensemble Framework for Hate Speech Detection in Bangla Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The proliferation of internet usage and social media platforms has significantly enhanced the ability of individuals to express their opinions on various topics. However, this freedom of expression sometimes morphs into a vehicle for disseminating hate speech, leading to increased incidents of cyberbullying, violations, and conflicts. Particularly on video-sharing websites, which have become a prominent stage for such activities due to their widespread use and the dynamic nature of video content. This study aims to address the issue of hate speech in video content by developing a robust method for detecting hate speech in Bangla language videos. The focus is on the spoken content within these videos, which is a primary vector for the transmission of harmful messages. We constructed a comprehensive dataset by extracting and converting audio from a collection of videos into text. Utilizing this dataset, we applied machine learning techniques and deep learning models to analyze and classify the content. Specifically, our approach involves a stacking ensemble model that combines the strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU) with the analytical capabilities of customized feature extraction applied to Multinomial Naive Bayes and Random Forest classifiers serving as a meta-model. The proposed stacking ensemble model demonstrates a high level of efficacy, achieving an accuracy rate of 96% in detecting hate speech within the tested video content. This performance indicates a significant advancement over existing methods, underlining the effectiveness of our hybrid, multi-model approach.

articleTitle: Enhancing Network Intrusion Detection in a Limited Labeled Data Scenario: An Active Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The Internet was originally developed to facilitate easier communication through digital devices. It has made our lives easier by providing means for communication and delivering digital resources anywhere and at any time in the world. However, the internet also exposes users to the risk of criminals exploiting various vulnerabilities in the internet system, launching sophisticated attacks to gain valuable information and hamper users’ lives. Henceforth, an effective intrusion detection system (IDS) is imperative for safeguarding the data and resources of users in the cyber world. This research aims to enhance semi-supervised IDS models by leveraging limited labeled data and unlabeled data and exploring innovative approaches to improve adaptability and accuracy in detecting known and emerging threats, particularly in scenarios with limited labeled data available. Our study uses the UNSW-NB15 dataset, and the results show that our suggested active learning-based semi-supervised model, which was created with 2000 labeled data, is better than the supervised model that uses the same number of labeled data. The proposed model achieved an accuracy score of 97.67% while existing studies achieved an accuracy score of 94.61%.

articleTitle: Binary Classification of Benign and Malignant Laryngeal Lesions Using Transfer Learning and Ensemble Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This paper presents a reliable classification approach for Laryngeal lesions using pre-trained models and sophisticated combining methods. The dataset includes 11,144 images from 210 patients, with 69% benign and 31% malignant lesions. The data preprocessing included standardization, augmentation, and normalization. When implemented in Google Colab, the stacked model was formed by combining ResNet50V2, MobileNetV3, and EfficientNetV2, with a test data accuracy of 93.76%. Future work should be focused on diversifying the dataset and collaborating with medical professionals to refine the classification approach continuously.

articleTitle: Computational Analysis of Deleterious Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) in the Human LCT Gene
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) significantly impact an individual's susceptibility and response to diseases and therapy. This study focused on predicting and characterizing harmful missense nonsynonymous SNPs (nsSNPs) in the LCT gene which is essential for lactose hydrolysis into glucose and galactose, using various computational methods. SIFT and PolyPhen v2 were used to investigate nsSNPs at first, then SNAP, PhD-SNP, SNPs & GO, and I-Mutant 2.0 were used to further assess those that were projected to be deleterious. The LCT gene and protein interaction network was investigated using GeneMANIA and STRING tools, and the protein secondary structure prediction was made using NetSurfP 2.0. MISSENSE 3D was utilized to evaluate the structural influence of polymorphisms, and SWISS-MODEL was employed to forecast the protein structures of both wild-type and variant forms. Seven possibly deleterious nsSNPs (R1587H, D1407N, D925N, F1798S, G1375R, R1254Q, and R975C) that lowered protein stability were found when TM-align computed RMSD and TM scores. The findings of this study, which pinpoint high-risk nsSNPs in the LCT gene, offer a strong basis for further experimental investigation and point to putative molecular targets for both therapeutic and diagnostic uses. These damaging nsSNPs may be employed as targets to therapeutics and diagnostics. This comprehensive approach lays the groundwork for future research and clinical applications in the field of genetics and personalized medicine.

articleTitle: Anemia prediction and classification of all classes with and without anemia patients using a machine learning model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Anemia has emerged as a significant public health issue, typically caused by various factors such as nutritional deficiencies, chronic diseases, and genetic conditions. Identifying individuals at risk for developing anemia presents a major challenge for doctors and public health experts, as different types of anemia are distinguished by unique characteristics. While a simple, affordable, and widely available laboratory test, the complete blood count (CBC), is commonly used to diagnose anemia, it cannot differentiate between the various types. Therefore, the goal of this study is to develop a machine learning model to predict and classify all types of anemia using machine learning algorithms. In medical science, accurate prognosis and classification are vital for halting disease progression and detecting early affected areas. Machine learning (ML) techniques are frequently employed to predict and classify disease susceptibility with high accuracy, serving as a valuable tool for doctors and specialists. In this work, four machine learning algorithms were trained on a dataset to diagnose anemia and non-anemia patients: support vector machine, random forest, decision tree, and extreme gradient boosting classifier models. The XGBoost classifier outperformed the others, utilizing 25 out of 29 features with an accuracy of 0.9998, a precision of 0.9969, a recall of 0.9951, and an F1-score of 0.9960.

articleTitle: A Robotic-based Remote Control Painting System for Exterior Walls of High-Rise Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Exterior painting of high-rise buildings is a challenging task. In our country, as well as in other countries of the world, this task is accomplished manually, which is risky and life-threatening for the workers. Researchers and industry experts are trying to find an automatic and robotic solution for the exterior painting of high-rise building walls. In this paper, we propose a solution to this problem. We design and implement a prototype for automatically painting the building walls' exteriors. A spray mechanism was introduced in the prototype that can move in four different directions (up-down and left-right). All the movements are achieved by using microcontroller-operated servo motors. Further, these components create a scope to upgrade the proposed remote-controlled system to a robotic system in the future. In the presented system, all the operations are controlled remotely from a smartphone interface. Bluetooth technology is used for remote communications. The suggested system is expected to improve productivity with better workplace safety.

articleTitle: Enhancing Intrusion Detection Capabilities in IoT Technologies through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Smart home systems, industrial automation, healthcare systems, and others have been ground sectors developed massively because of the exponential growth that the Internet of Things (IoT) has had. The significant issues that it has presented are security challenges. IoT devices are weakly defended in terms of security and widely susceptible to cyber threats because of interconnectivity. This paper presents novel methods to mitigate such risks, with their implementation focused on intrusion detection systems that can be enhanced with Random Forest classifiers to detect and terminate malicious activities. The approach presented attains excellent performance, with an accuracy of 98.2% in the case of the NSL-KDD dataset and 99.9% for the BoT-IoT dataset. The paper discloses improved accuracy, precision, and recall relative to the existing approaches in the field and that RF classifiers effectively enhance the IDS capability. The importance of flexibility among ML models is therefore highlighted in the real-time detection and reaction to prevent significant damages and data breaches in IoT environments. The paper also discusses the deployment alternatives because of the limitation of resources in IoT devices, with which an architectural implementation of the IDS framework will raise challenges toward real-world IoT applications. Effective methods for overhead and accurate detection efficacy were also recommended. These results are regarded as an addition to the debate on IoT security and have been helpful to researchers, practitioners, and policymakers. This state-of-the-art machine learning technique is protection proposed for the IoT ecosystem not only from present threats but also from futuristic challenges to ensure the most secure IoT systems. Research contributes to innovation and continuous improvement by securing a growing IoT and future advanced systems through cyber collaboration

articleTitle: An Efficient Integrated Negative Fractional Counting Sort Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The time complexity of the Counting Sort algorithm is linear and is famous for sorting non-negative integers (0−positive). It runs well for a possible small difference between the smallest and largest number in the input data series to avoid redundant unused memory space. So far studied in the literature, the traditional counting sort algorithm may also be applied to sort all integers (negative-0-positive) in such a way that positive and negative integers will be dealt with separately to sort. In this paper, we propose a integrated form of counting sort algorithm to sort all real numbers and we call it the "negative fractional counting sort" method that can efficiently sort arrays with negative and positive integers along with fractional numbers. While the input array has been extended from the integer range (0toK) to the fractional range from –ve fractional number to +ve fractional number, the time complexity remains linear. The proposed method involves separately sorting the negative and positive components of the array, followed by an innovative merging process. This integrated approach eliminates the need for additional arrays or multiple sorting passes, thus optimizing memory usage and computational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm’s capability to sort mixed numeric arrays effectively, with performance metrics indicating minimal execution time. Our contribution offers a versatile and efficient sorting solution, extending the practical utility of Counting Sort to a broader spectrum of real-world data scenarios.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Multi-Load Handling MAC Protocol for WBAN Based on IEEE 802.15.6 Standard Using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The capacity to exchange data and provide real-time monitoring for patient care makes wireless body area networks (WBANs) vital for modern medical treatment systems. WBANs are used for various traffic loads, including high-rate and extremely low-rate continuous monitoring data. The communication standard of IEEE-802.15.6 describes physical and MAC layer functions for WBANs. The IEEE 802.15.6 superframe is used to handle multiple types of traffic load in WBAN based on predefined user priorities. Since various kinds of data traffic have fixed periods, this results in an ineffective use of the superframe. In this study, we develop a multi-class multi-load handling MAC (MMH-MAC) protocol for WBANs. This protocol maximizes the use of the IEEE 802.15.6 superframe through reinforcement learning (i.e., Q-learning). The proposed MAC protocol classifies the data, calculates the node’s Q-value, and allocates the time slot for different loads based on the largest Q-value using the TDMA technique. The operation of the MMH-MAC protocol is examined via comprehensive NS-2 simulations and thoroughly contrasted with the present protocols.

articleTitle: Unleashing Machine Learning for Hepatitis C Prediction: A Holistic Exploration of Clinical Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Chronic diseases, characterized by long-term effects and persistent symptoms, pose significant challenges to human health and well-being. The hepatitis C virus (HCV) is the cause of chronic hepatitis C, which affects 58 million people globally. It also causes 290,000 deaths annually due to liver cancer and cirrhosis, two conditions connected to HCV. Taking advantage of machine learning (ML) algorithms' ability to analyze large datasets and identify patterns and relationships that aid in diagnosis, this effort focuses on employing algorithms for machine learning to identify and forecast hepatitis C precisely. Various techniques were utilized, including Random Forest, Cat Boost, SVM, and others to create predictive models using blood values from 615 patients, including both hepatitis patients and healthy blood donors. The dataset underwent comprehensive preprocessing, including handling missing values, scaling, and dimensionality reduction via Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Various ML algorithms were evaluated, and the Cat Boost classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 99.17%, recall of 92.00%, precision of 100.00% and F1-score is 96.00%. This study demonstrates the potential of ML in enhancing HCV diagnosis, offering less invasive and cost-effective alternatives to traditional methods, and providing predictive insights for personalized treatment plans. The findings underscore the importance of advanced data preprocessing and feature selection in improving model efficiency. This study adds to the ongoing efforts to lessen the prevalence of hepatitis C worldwide, aligning with the World Health Organization's goal to significantly decrease new HCV cases and related deaths by 2030.

articleTitle: Predictive Wake-Up Based Optimized MAC Protocol Design for Underwater Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The Underwater Wireless Sensor Network (UWSN) provides an effective way of communicating in aquatic environments to overcome the constraints of applying terrestrial MAC protocols. Due to unique challenges and requirements of underwater communication, designing specialized MAC protocols for UWSNs is crucial to conserve energy. Currently, research has focused on duty-cycled receiver-initiated asynchronous MAC protocols due to their superior performance over sender-initiated protocols and their ability to overcome the challenges of synchronous MAC protocols. However, existing UWSN MAC protocols suffer from re-transmissions, energy loss, protocol overheads, and longer duty-cycle periods. This paper proposes a MAC protocol for UWSNs, termed Predictive Wake-Up Based Optimized MAC (PWO-MAC) protocol, which incorporates an additive increase and multiplicative decrease (AIMD) technique along with a predictive wake-up scheduling approach. The proposed PWO-MAC protocol dynamically adjusts transmission rates, enabling re-transmissions only upon failure and reducing multiple transmission. The protocol optimizes protocol overhead, reduces energy consumption, ensures minimum delay and enhances network throughput.

articleTitle: Creating Multi-level AI Racing Agents Using a Combination of Imitation and Reinforcement Learning and Analyzing Similarity Using Cross-Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This study explores creating AI opponents for a basic car racing game using Unreal Engine 5 (UE5). The main goal is to make AI opponents that act like human players, giving gamers a fun challenge. To do this, we combined imitation learning and reinforcement learning. With imitation learning, we gathered data from players of different skill levels and used it to teach AI how to race like them. We divided players into five groups based on their skills, from beginners to experts. Then, we trained AI to copy the racing styles of each group, making AI opponents of different difficulties. Alongside imitation learning, we used reinforcement learning to improve AI racing skills. We rewarded good behaviors, like staying on the track, and punished bad ones, like veering off. This helped AI learn the best racing strategies. We also compared AI performance to human players. By analyzing how closely AI matched each player group’s style, we could see how well the AI performed. Results showed that combining imitation and reinforcement learning made AI opponents that behaved like human players. By adjusting learning settings, we made AI opponents at different difficulty levels, giving gamers a personalized challenge. This study shows how simple machine learning techniques can enhance racing game experiences without using complex algorithms. It demonstrates the potential of blending learning methods to make games more enjoyable.

articleTitle: An Effective Deep Learning Approach for Kidney Stone Detection in CT Scan Images using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Kidney stones represent a significant global health concern, frequently causing individuals to seek immediate medical care due to intense pain. Radiological imaging modalities are one of the most common modes of diagnosis, but specialist interpretation is always important for accuracy. In this paper, we present computer vision in an automated kidney stone detection system that involves five stages: loading the dataset, preprocessing data, loading the InceptionV3 model, predicting, and evaluating performance. Various methods of preprocessing and data augmentation were utilized to make the model less biased and more robust. This study uses the InceptionV3 architecture to classify kidney stones in CT scan images of KUB (Kidney, Ureter, and Bladder). We utilize a total dataset of 433 participants, either diagnosed with kidney stones or in a normal state. 278 cases are diagnosed with kidney stones, and 165 are normal cases. The proposed approach achieved an impressive 98.55% accuracy across performance metrics when evaluated on an independent test dataset.

articleTitle: A Study on Drug Addiction Prediction in Bangladeshi Universities Using Advanced Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Infection by alcohol and drugs has become one of the bigger dangers posed to the youth of Bangladesh, and responsible action on the part of society is called for in order to save these tender minds. In a bid to solve this problem, a study was conducted on reducing drug abuse using machine learning concepts. The data were gathered from 307 students, wherein there are drug users and non-users aged between 17-35, with the final dataset containing 21 features. Hence, the strategy for drug abusers can be predicted with the probability of an individual's addiction to drugs by designing a machine learning strategy. It is based on the consultations and opinions obtained from medical professionals and drug addicts, together with literature reviews, that key risk factors of addiction are suggested in the present study. The collected data was pre-processed and fed for four machine learning algorithms: logistic regression, SVM, naïve Bayes, and XGBoost. The performances of each classifier, as evaluated by some of the notable metrics, turned out to be: 95.16% for SVM, 93.55% for logistic regression, 96.77% for naïve Bayes, and 98.39% for XGBoost. The present research informs about the prospects of machine learning for risk assessment in drug addiction among the youth of Bangladesh and contributes to more effective prevention strategies. The main goal of this research is to develop predictive models to identify a person's risk of drug addiction based on behavioral, social and health factors. It can be an early intervention, prevention effort and help to improve its condition.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Using Support Vector Machines and Advanced Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: A major cause of illness and mortality on a global scale is Cardiovascular Disease (CVD). Ensuring timely response and efficient management requires precise risk prediction. This study rigorously examines the use of support vector machines (SVM) and other advanced machine learning algorithms to opti-mize cardiovascular risk prediction. The authors have obtained a comprehensive dataset comprising patient gender analysis, patient behavior, and medical history parameters from a diverse patient cohort. The dataset has been meticulously preprocessed to impute missing values and accurately welcome and encode attributes. There were multiple machine learning models that were utilized, including SVM, random forest, and XG boosting, to forecast the likelihood of future cardiovascular events. This study’s key contributions include: (1) developing an optimized SVM model for cardiovascular risk prediction that outperforms traditional methods, (2) comprehensively comparing multiple advanced machine learning algorithms, and (3) introducing a novel approach to handling imbalanced data in cardiovascular risk assessment. The results unequivocally demonstrate that SVM, with its kernel technique and margin optimization, delivers superior performance in accuracy, precision, and recall compared to traditional logistic regression models. Ensemble methods such as Random Forest and XG Boosting are essential for managing imbalanced data and performing thorough feature importance analysis in data science and machine learning. This will enable doctors to easily understand each feature in predicting risk. In conclusion, the integration of machine learning algorithms, especially SVMs, into cardiovascular risk prediction frameworks can significantly enhance their predictive power. These advances have the potential to revolutionize CVD risk stratification and pave the way for personalized medicine, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: LightNN: An Optimized Deep Learning Framework for Enhanced Fruit Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The crucial field of fruit classification in computer vision and deep learning brings about breakthroughs that have broad applications in the retail and agricultural industries. By automating the identification and sorting of various fruit types, these technologies enhance efficiency, accuracy, and scalability, benefiting processes from farm production to market distribution. The integration of sophisticated algorithms and neural networks not only improves the speed and reliability of fruit classification but also offers the potential for real-time quality control and inventory management, revolutionizing traditional methods and paving the way for more innovative, data-driven approaches in these sectors. This study introduces LightNN, a novel and effective paradigm with a lightweight architecture that tackles the complex problems related to computational efficiency. Combining a small classifier with a simplified feature extractor, LightNN achieves the ideal balance between simplicity and accuracy. The feature extractor is capable of extracting hierarchical features from RGB images by using convolutional layers with ReLU activations and max-pooling procedures. The flattened output is then processed by the classifier, which consists of fully connected layers with ReLU activations and dropout regularisation. Remarkably, LightNN, with just 298,835 parameters, manages to get a respectable 96.37% test accuracy in fruit categorization tasks. The results highlight LightNN’s promise as an effective and efficient fruit classifying method, particularly in situations with constrained computational resources.

articleTitle: IoT Based Smart Waste Monitoring System Envisioning a Sustainable Smart City
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This paper introduces a smart approach to waste management through the integration of smart technologies. Our proposed system employs the ESP8266 Wi-Fi module to enable remote notification, ensuring efficient waste monitoring both indoors and outdoors. The core components include an Ultrasonic Sensor HC-SR04 for real-time monitoring of the waste bin's fill level, an IR sensor to facilitate automated lid opening upon user proximity, and a servo motor to control the lid mechanism. Upon detection of fullness of the waste bin, the system triggers a buzzer, providing an audible alert for the user and encouraging the user timely waste disposal. The innovation aimed for a more cost effective and economically beneficial system. The innovation extends beyond conventional waste monitoring because we are not only implementing it indoors but also outdoors to monitor waste disposal which will maintain a clean environment overall. The paper outlines the implementation of a client-server model, emphasizing its potential to foster a pollution-free society, good health, and a cleaner environment.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Machine Learning Classifiers for Early Diagnosis of Cervical Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Cervical cancer is a significant worldwide health issue, particularly in underdeveloped countries where the availability of preventive healthcare treatments is restricted. Effective prevention and treatment of cervical cancer depend on early recognition of the disease's threats. Machine-learning algorithms have become popular in recent years as promising methods of diagnosing cancer risk based on medical and demographic data. This study looks to observe the way algorithms based on machine learning might be applied to estimate the risk of cervical cancer with a dataset that includes patient demographics, clinical history, and diagnostic test findings. Predictive systems are created using several machine learning approaches, such as Decision Tree, Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting, Nearest Centroid, Multilayer Perceptron, and AdaBoost. These model's prediction powers are evaluated using performance criteria including accuracy, sensitivity, precision, f-measure, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC). Our findings indicate that the decision tree achieved the maximum accuracy, precision, and f1-score (98.91%, 97.81%, and 0.9889, respectively). Furthermore, hyperparameter tuning was used to optimize model performance. For instance, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) attained a remarkable accuracy of 99.27%, precision of 98.53%, and F1-score following hyperparameter adjustment of 0.9926, demonstrating its potential in cervical cancer chance prediction. This demonstrates the possibilities and capability of machine learning methods in improving correct predicting as well as patient outcomes for cervical cancer detection.

articleTitle: Grainbee: A Quantum-Resistant Blockchain-Based Ration Distribution System with Hardware Security Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In developing countries, subsidized food programs aimed at supporting the poor are often undermined by corruption and mismanagement, leading to food waste and unequal distribution. To overcome these challenges, we introduce GrainBee, a blockchain-powered ration distribution system designed to ensure secure, transparent, and efficient food supply distribution. By leveraging blockchain’s inherent security and immutability, GrainBee addresses the major security and transparency issues that plague traditional and existing blockchain-based systems.Our proposed system employs a post-quantum secure, blockchain-based approach to combat corruption and fraudulent invoicing, guaranteeing integrity through a distributed, immutable ledger. To further fortify security, we integrate Hardware Security Modules (HSMs), providing an additional layer of protection for sensitive data and transactions. A built-in reservation and scheduling system streamlines the distribution process, while a user-friendly interface and machine translation services bridge language gaps, enhancing usability and accessibility. By harnessing the power of blockchain technology, GrainBee offers a robust solution to the complex challenges of food distribution.

articleTitle: Diabetes Prediction Using Machine Learning and Hybrid Deep Learning Ensemble Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Diabetes prediction is an essential task of healthcare which enables early diagnosis and treatment. In this study, we present a comprehensive analysis utilizing machine learning and ensemble deep learning techniques for diabetes prediction, leveraging two distinct datasets: such as the PIMA diabetes dataset which contains 768 records with 9 attributes, and another diabetes dataset which has exactly 2000 records with 9 attributes. The approach that we have adopted for cleaning up data has a lot of prerequisites, aimed at achieving accuracy. We applied a preprocessing technique for removing duplicates and replacing zero values with the mean or median. In addition to that, we applied the scaling process known as standardization on our given data, it is a method that ensures the average of all the values is 0 and the standard deviation is 1. To process our input finding, we implemented a set of machine learning algorithms covering K Nearest Neighbors, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression along with ensemble deep learning techniques of TabNet, XGBoost, and Multilayer Perceptron which shows the best possible outcomes. The proposed hybrid deep learning ensemble approach presents the best results for predicting diabetes. In our research hybrid deep learning ensemble technique has accuracy of 96%, this method shows much higher efficiency over common machine learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Stress Analysis in Social Media in Bengali language using BERT-based approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Recent researches highlight a rapid increase in mental health issues, signaling a concerning rise in stress-related conditions such as high blood pressure, psoriasis, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), etc., and these should have a sophisticated remedy that plays a big role in stress analysis. To proceed with that the ongoing connection between increased stress levels and social media has gained a lot of attention. This study focused on inspecting a complex language, Bengali by extracting comments from YouTube to analyze stress to provide a meaningful solution. We are aware of no research on stress analysis in the Bengali language, although many studies have been done on the same topic in other languages. Thus by paying closer attention to stress analysis in the Bengali language, our work suggested a BERT-based method that has shown good results on a range of NLP tasks. Our approach included Bangla-BERT-base and hybrid models that combine deep and transfer learning, like BERT-LSTM, BERT-GRU, and BERT-CNN-BiLSTM. Our task performed well with an accuracy of 90.36% in stress analysis utilizing the Bengali dataset. Our experiment also helped to get an understanding that hybrid models had an influence in increasing the performance of the BERT-base model. Though our research has made little contribution to the BNLP field considering its vast aspect, expanding the Bengali dataset and conducting further multi-class stress analysis work can have a remarkable contribution.

articleTitle: Optimizing Waste Reduction Through Real-Time Defect Detection in Garment Sewing Using Variants YOLOv7
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In the era of computer vision to overcome challenges, the introduction of the YOLO model revolutionized real-time computer vision approaches. In the garment industry, the inception of products plays a significant role while increasing the processing time with a good accuracy rate is the big challenge here. A real-time garments defect detection approach using YOLOv7, YOLOv7x, and YOLOv7-w6 on a primary dataset is proposed with a good FPS rate and better accuracy. Maximum traditional garments inception approaches focused on end product defects while this model suggests detecting defects in the sewing phase so that the cost of the rejected end product can be optimized by detecting them before a product goes through all the phases. For this our research focuses on three subclasses of Seam, Stitch, and Hole related to sewing phase defects. To increase the detection rate, the hyperparameter tuning technique is applied to the YOLOv7 model. Three models are proposed based on pre-trained weights of YOLOv7, YOLOv7x, and YOLOv7-w6 to compare the accuracy and FPS rate in terms of implementation in real-world projects.

articleTitle: Combining Ensemble Learning based Hybrid Classification Algorithm with Effective Feature Selection to identify Electricity Fraud in Advanced Metering Infrastructure of Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Consuming electricity through Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) has become an irrefutable part of our daily micro-moments. In AMI, electricity fraud is regarded as one of the most significant Nontechnical losses (NTLs) for power companies which requires substantial investigation to effectively detect theft instances with minimal false positives. In this paper, we investigated how the meticulous selection of top-ranked attributes enhances the accuracy of fraud identification. We proposed a modified-ReliefF feature selection algorithm to find the rank of attributes of our developed dataset and observed significant improvement in electricity fraud identification. Moreover, we designed a hybrid classifier called ElectroGuard SVM Bagging, which combines SVM with Bootstrap Aggregation. This approach, paired with our modified-ReliefF feature selection, outperformed three standard supervised classifiers. Finally, using 10-fold cross-validation, we compared our hybrid model’s performance against the best result obtaining conventional classifier, i.e. SVM and achieved 5.94% (before applying feature selection) and 6.19% (after applying modified-ReliefF feature selection) accuracy improvement for ElectroGuard SVM Bagging.

articleTitle: Single-Level Fusion for Enhancing Meat Quality Classification with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Growing the global meat market, especially in the Asia-Pacific region, also brought a desire to continue providing quality meats, and this implies the need to invest in a high-quality meat supply to avoid health issues associated with spoiled meat like stomach upsets and food poisoning. This study proposes a state-of-the-art deep-learning model of a single fusion level of ConvNeXtTiny and DenseNet169 networks for categorizing meat as fresh, half-fresh, and spoiled. Pivotal to this study is the use of Grad-CAM++ for explainable AI (XAI) that offers finer localization by generating high-resolution heatmaps that focus on the important regions in images. This approach enhances the interpretability of the model’s decision-making process in a way that enables users to determine which of the features contributes to classification results easily. The model, trained on a comprehensive dataset of 10,931 images, achieved a notable testing accuracy of 97.46%, outperforming recent studies. Therefore, besides demonstrating the effectiveness of the chosen XAI techniques, this study contributes to enhancing the safety and quality of meat products by providing insightful explanations of the operations of the AI system.

articleTitle: Effective Object Detection in Hyperspectral Images using Segmentation and Multibranch 2D-3D CNN Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In spite of the improvement of the Hyperspectral Image classification using a convolutional neural network, lesser training samples limit the classification performance. While 3D CNNs can extract combined spectral-spatial characteristics but need more complicated models, traditional 2-D CNN approaches underutilize the interband correlations in HSIs. Combining 3D-2D CNN multibranch feature fusion can take advantage of both the 3D and 2D CNN. Our proposed method implements Segmented Principal Component analysis (SPCA), minimum-Redundancy-Maximum-Relevance (mRMR) to exploit the local structure of the data and rank the features to form groups based on their significance. To extract the features as efficiently as possible, the shallow branch carries the least significant features, and the deep branch carries the top features. Our suggested model works better than the existing ones, attaining noteworthy accuracy of 99.12%, 99.94% and 100% on Indian Pines, University of Pavia and Salinas Scene datasets respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Spam Email Detection with a Soft Voting Ensemble of Optimized Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Spam email detection is crucial for cybersecurity, as it protects user privacy and reduces security risks. The persistent presence of spammers necessitates continuous improvements in spam filtering measures. To address this challenge, this study employs Grid Search Optimizer to fine-tune the parameters of four distinct classifiers: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, Naive Bayes, and XGBoost. Soft Voting serves as the final classifier, enhancing overall accuracy by integrating results from optimized classifiers to detect and classify spam emails across the Spam Mails Dataset and Enron1 Dataset. The experimental study compared the proposed model with relevant works and found that hyperparameter tuning and Soft Voting significantly enhanced its performance compared to existing approaches. The proposed ensemble model outperformed individual classifiers, achieving accuracies of 99.32% and 99.12%, respectively. Also, the ensemble model demonstrated an AUC of 1.00 on both datasets, indicating its effectiveness in distinguishing between spam and ham emails. This approach surpasses prior studies in accuracy, generalization, and robustness by innovatively combining Grid Search and Soft Voting. The constructed model exhibits high effectiveness and efficiency in the detection of spam emails.

articleTitle: PAKE – PoS Tagger Augmented Keyword Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The state-of-the-art techniques for automatic keyword extraction majorly deal with the collection of long documents. However, for several reasons, these do not provide satisfactory results for shorter lengths of documents. Moreover, with the ever-increasing amounts of information available, a keyword extraction system that automatically deals with varying lengths of text can lessen the workload and make the entire process of manually assigning the keywords less time-consuming. For this, the widely used Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques are examined in the context of extensive data. Therefore, this research introduces PAKE - PoStagger Augmented Keyword Extraction system as a practical amalgamation of statistical and textual-based features based on an unsupervised key phrase extracting algorithm to stand out as a suitable alternative to the existing solutions. The effectiveness is demonstrated by comparing it with six state-of-the-art unsupervised methods, and the results are illustrated using four datasets.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Network Architecture to Predict Supercontinuum Generation in Chalcogenide-Silica Hybrid Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In this paper, we have introduced a novel deep learning approach as an efficient alternative to conventional numerical simulations for predicting supercontinuum generation in a chalcogenide-silica hybrid Photonic Crystal Fiber. Traditional simulations performed in COMSOL Multiphysics and subsequent supercontinuum spectrum analysis in MATLAB are computationally intensive and time-consuming. Our proposed Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) model, trained from scratch, demonstrates impressive accuracy in forecasting supercontinuum spectral bandwidth, achieving a mean square error of 0.00078784. This accuracy enables us to effectively map the optical characteristics of our model. Our results position the RNN model as a fast and accurate alternative to conventional numerical calculations for predicting supercontinuum spectral bandwidth. By significantly reducing computational time, our model enables rapid predictions of supercontinuum spectra, benefiting early cancer cell detection, frequency metrology, optical coherence tomography, spectroscopy, and hazardous material sensing. This is, to the authors' knowledge, the first exploration of supercontinuum generation using an RNN model in PCF.

articleTitle: A Semi-Supervised Approach For Detecting Agricultural Land Reduction In Bangladesh Using Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Recently, remote sensing change detection has significantly improved because of greater access to global satellite images and developments in satellite technology. Several CNN-based techniques have demonstrated exceptional precision. Detecting the amount of agricultural area that has been reduced is a type of change detection problem that can easily be solved using deep learning methods on satellite data. But the majority of deep learning methods have been specifically created for high-resolution images. This data lacks global coverage, consists of at most 3 to 4 bands, and is costly. The Sentinel-2 satellite, which was launched in 2015, offers medium-resolution multi-spectral image data consisting of 14 bands and provides free global coverage. Having more bands enhances the capabilities for model analysis. But there is a lack of labeled satellite data. This research proposes a semi-supervised method for generating ground truth by employing a multi-step procedure. This technique began with semi-supervised classification to label the images, followed by a sequence of refinement processes to enhance the accuracy of the ground truth mask. The mask was created using the XGBoost machine learning technique. The dataset was assessed using the output images generated by the trained model. Detecting changes in low-resolution image may be difficult, but proposed method will greatly streamline the procedure. Applying this approach revealed an approximately 8.35% decrease in agricultural land area inside the test image area between 2018 and 2022. In the test area of 237.77 square kilometers, the reduced area measures approximately 19.861 square kilometers.

articleTitle: Enhanced Detection of DoS/DDoS Attacks in SDN Using Ensemble and Hybrid CNN-LSTM Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) faces significant challenges in mitigating Attacks known as denial of service (DoS) and distributed DDoS due to its centralized control plane architecture. This centralization makes the control plane an attractive target for attackers, highlighting the need for effective detection and mitigation strategies. In this study, we propose three innovative methodologies to enhance the accuracy of detecting DoS/DDoS attacks in SDN environments. Our first methodology employs an ensemble model with a voting classifier, which achieves a detection accuracy of 97.4%. This approach leverages multiple weak learners to enhance the robustness of detection. The second methodology utilizes an ensemble with a stacking technique, attaining a superior accuracy of 99%, demonstrating the efficacy of integrating multiple base models in a hierarchical fashion. The third approach introduces a novel hybrid model that blends LSTM networks with CNN, achieving a competitive accuracy of 98.51%. A comparative analysis of these methods reveals that, while all three significantly enhance detection rates, the stacking ensemble technique outperforms the others. This finding underscores the potential of advanced ensemble techniques in effectively addressing the dynamic and evolving cyber threats within SDN environments. Our study offers valuable insights into strengthening SDN infrastructures against DoS/DDoS attacks, contributing to the ongoing efforts to secure modern network architectures.

articleTitle: Hinglish Products Review-Based Sentiment Analysis on Using Ml Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In the realm of e-commerce, understanding consumer sentiment towards products is paramount for businesses to thrive. With the exponential growth of online shopping in India, an increasing number of customers express their opinions through a blend of Hindi and English, commonly known as Hinglish. This study delves into the domain of sentiment analysis, focusing specifically on Hinglish product reviews, and employs machine learning (ML) algorithms to decipher the sentiments expressed within these reviews. The research aims to develop a robust framework capable of accurately categorizing Hinglish product reviews into positive, negative, or neutral sentiments. The proposed framework leverages NLP to preprocess and analyze Hinglish text data. This preprocessing stage includes tokenization, stemming, and eliminating stop words in order to extract significant characteristics from the text. The system then utilizes machine learning algorithms including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naive Bayes, and Random Forest to train sentiment categorization models. The training datasets for these models consist of labeled datasets, including Hinglish product reviews, each annotated with sentiment polarity. Iterative sentiment analysis applied to Hinglish product reviews has important ramifications for enterprises in the Indian market. Through effective identification of client attitudes, organizations can acquire substantial knowledge regarding customer preferences, degrees of satisfaction, and prospects for enhancement. As a result, businesses are better equipped to customize their product offerings, marketing campaigns, and customer support programs to better suit the demands and preferences of their target market. I used new conceptual data in the Hindi language but English alphabet format. I have used ten models here. I am trying to find out the best accuracy models among them. ExtraTree best performance at 93% accuracy, Random Forest 92.13% and SVM 91.71% model with accuracy.

articleTitle: Predicting Preterm Birth Among South-Asian Women Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Preterm Birth remains one of the preventable yet large contributors to child and maternal mortality. Despite progress in reducing infant mortality, South Asia continues to report a significant number of preterm birth-related deaths annually. Moreover, those who survive have to bear the long-term impact of physical and neurological disabilities - especially low-income households who are unable to afford healthcare. This study aims to offer a prediction model that can predict preterm birth using social, physical and health records of South-Asian women. Traditional models such as Decision Trees, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, Logistic Regression and neural network-based deep learning models such as Multilayer Perceptron are used to compare the models’ AUC, F1 scores and accuracy points. Random Forest generated the highest accuracy and F1 score (89%), whereas Multilayer Perceptron generated the best AUC score (88%) and had an overall consistent performance. Further analysis revealed the main factors contributing to preterm birth were weight before pregnancy, age and BMI of the mother.

articleTitle: Credibility Analysis of Robot Speech Based on Bangla Language Dialect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Our daily life now largely depends on the assistance of different machines. We perform various tasks using machines which make our lives easier. As machines are getting closer to having a perfect imitation of the human voice, it’s very important to give machines enough credibility for different cultural settings. Our research tends to find the robot speech’s credibility in persuasiveness in the context of different factors that affect credibility as well as local dialects of Bangladesh. From the previous research, we found that practical knowledge-based speech and rhetoric cues can increase the credibility of speech. It is also seen that these element’s importance can vary from culture to culture. Our research is based on previous studies where they tried to estimate robot speech credibility in different languages [1].We have performed three studies. One study is to find the effect of knowledge and rhetoric linguistics on the credibility of a robot that speaks in Bangla. Next is to find the effect of credibility based on accents. In both of these studies, standard Bangla shows the go-to option while making the speech credible. To understand why it is feaver over other accents of Bangla we conducted a third survey where we selected five Bangladeshi local dialects such as Jessore, Sylheti, Chittagong, Barisal, and formal Chalito dialect to perform our study. We assessed the credibility of the speech when the robot’s voice had accents of these given dialects while talking. Our research is based on the survey we conducted to understand the significance of accents in robot speech. Our major findings give us an idea about the most credible Bengali accent and their feedback about using local accents in robot speech. Most participants are open to using the local dialects in robot speech as a secondary option. From these results, it can be concluded that, although local dialects are welcomed by the people, they still feel uncomfortable using them for convenient use while interacting with a machine for important work. The results acquired from the experiment can be useful to improve the user experience in the context of human computer interaction across Bengali culture.

articleTitle: Enhancing Parallelism in Cross-silo Federated Learning for Brain Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The brain is essential for regulating various bodily processes, and preserving its well-being is crucial for a good quality of life. Disorders like Alzheimer’s disease and brain tumors significantly impact individuals’ lives. Traditional centralized learning methods, such as machine learning and deep learning, have demonstrated improved performance in detecting these diseases. However, a major concern in the present day is the inability of centralized learning to protect the privacy of subjects’ data. To address it, this paper focuses on privacy-preserving cross-silo federated learning for detecting Alzheimer’s disease and brain tumors. The LeNet5 model, with the Adam and SGD optimizers, analyzes T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data and achieves an average of 95% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score for Alzheimer’s disease classification with 90% and 100% client participation. For brain tumor classification, a mean accuracy of 94.66%, and precision, recall, and F1 score of 95% are achieved using the LeNet5 with SGD optimizer. Our findings also manifest that it is very challenging to determine the percentage of client participation required to achieve a moderate or better performance in cross-silo federated learning since the result fluctuates but it is clear that about a minimum of 20% of client participation is required in case of balanced or mostly balanced dataset.

articleTitle: Smart water the development method using iot and blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is used in all intelligent functions as a fully created and firmly established technique that will be present in the next Internet waves. Similar to the Internet of Things, blockchain is a growing technology that uses a distributed register to improve the protection of each blockchain node. Any flawed operation on the blockchain technology is not carried out by unauthorized users. The Internet of Things and the block-chain are integrated to enhance the efficiency of applications that operate in real-time. In this study, an innovative water handling method based on IOT is developed for agricultural, ensuring the efficacy of water administration for farming. This is accomplished via the use of autonomous surveillance using the Internet of Things (IoT). The supervision and oversight of the agricultural water were carried out by integrating with 2D modeling. subsequently, an approach for managing irrigation water used for farming is put into place via the collecting of information in real-time. The resulting data is shown, and it refreshes the water tracking dashboard every various number of hours. The current water-related architecture makes use of IoT and autonomous surveillance technologies. This is a highly effective method for the administration of water supplies as well as the provision of water.

articleTitle: PV Powered Smart Irrigation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The research conducted in this study focuses on examining the viability of renewable energy sources as an alternative means of generating electricity in off-grid areas. This study demonstrates the optimal design of a photovoltaic (PV) drip irrigation system, emphasizing key considerations for tailoring the system to a specific geographic location. The design involves calculations of motor power, solar irradiance, and meteorological factors. A simulation study assesses potential power generation by optimizing tilt angles and orientations of PV modules, accounting for monthly and annual variations, overall shading, and internal shading used between component rows. The water pump and motor are selected based on the water table depth, intended discharge, and head for effective irrigation. The paper introduces a solar-powered portable water pump (SPWP) for a smart irrigation system. The system oversees and manages the water pump using Arduino, moisture sensors, and floating sensors. A user-friendly LCD takes center stage, prominently featuring a counter for automatic pump activations. This counter is specifically linked to the float sensor, which triggers the pump to fill the tank during automatic mode. Each activation increments the counter, giving users a clear count of automatic pump operations. The pump is powered by a solar panel, contributing to energy efficiency and reduced operational costs. Integration of portable water pump usage efficiency enables convenient and real-time monitoring and control. The system has undergone practical testing in a real-world setting, affirming its performance and validating its efficacy in enhancing agricultural operations.

articleTitle: Exploring Soil pH Variability: Statistical Analysis and Machine Learning Models for Enhanced Soil Health Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Soil pH is a crucial parameter for soil health and fertility. To understand the impact of different soil elements on pH is vital for effectively managing soil health. Our paper revolves around the relationship between soil pH and various nutrients such as organic matter, Nitrogen Nitrate, Phosphorus, potassium, iron, magnesium, manganese, zinc along with physical properties including sand, clay, silt, salinity. Furthermore, statistical analysis is extensively used to predict soil pH, assess nutrient interdependency, and other correlations between relevant variables. Our study provides a comprehensive analysis of soil pH prediction using Z-test, T-test, Simple Linear regression, and ANOVA test yielding valuable insights. Afterward, a correlation heatmap was formulated to explore the relationships among the features. The models were trained with highly correlated features and achieved expected prediction for the Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine(SVM), and Polynomial Regression model.
