Furthermore, SHAP(Shapley Additive Explanation) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) were applied for more comprehensive visualization of the predicted models. In conclusion, It is proven that increasing R2-score value (90.591) and decreasing MSE (0.078) with the inclusion of more features indicate that the models effectively capture the intricate relationships between soil pH and nutrients, leading to a more precise prediction.

articleTitle: Advancement of Drug Discovery Using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The current boom in artificial intelligence and machine learning has significantly reduced human labor and greatly improved quality of life. This paper explores how AI and ML are being applied to streamline drug discovery and development, enhancing both efficiency and accuracy. Nevertheless, the limited effectiveness, distribution to unintended targets, time-consuming nature, and exorbitant expenses provide significant obstacles and difficulties that affect the process of drug design and development. The study involved an extensive literature review of numerous research articles and effectively highlight and discuss about the application of various advanced algorithms for drug discovery. The study highlighted how AI and ML contribute to reducing the time and cost associated with drug development and discovery. These technologies allow for the use of simulations, which can potentially obviate the need for clinical trials, and enable researchers to conduct extensive studies on various compounds without experimental trials. The results illustrate the extensive application of AI and ML in drug discovery, indicating a promising future for these technologies. They hold significant potential for further exploration and application in drug discovery and development by researchers, students, and the pharmaceutical industry. Finally, the progress in AI and deep learning presents a promising chance for the rational development and exploration of drugs, ultimately benefiting humanity.

articleTitle: CSI-Based People Counting in WiFi Networks: Leveraging Occupancy Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The use of WiFi-based techniques to identify human activity has significantly increased in the past few years. The growing interest in smart buildings, retail analytics, healthcare facilities, and public spaces where real-time occupancy monitoring is essential. Detecting occupancy levels using Wi-fi is a great option because it is available almost everywhere. In wireless communications, the term "channel state information" (CSI) refers to the known channel properties of a communication link. CSI data can be used to implement object detection, human activity detection, patient activity monitoring, and so on. This work presents a framework for estimating the occupancy of an indoor environment, like a lab, inside a car, meeting room, using WiFi Channel State Information. The framework consists of four main steps: hardware configuration, CSI data collection, data preprocessing, and the number of people prediction. Qualcomm Atheros AR5BMD222 Wi-Fi LAN card TX-5B222 having a double antenna were used as both the transmitter and receiver. The raw CSI data have been collected from one person to five people, increasing gradually. During the preprocessing step, null subcarriers were eliminated, and amplitude and phase data were extracted and converted into decibels. Then the normalization was performed on the dataset. CSI data is Sequential Data. Therefore, there will be reliance on the datasets. CNN and LSTM architecture are used which combines the strengths of both networks to effectively extract features, model sequential information, and capture complex relationships in WiFi signals for accurate crowd counting in multi-human environments. We have trained classification models and achieved overall accuracy rates of 98.12%, 96.88%, 95.75%, 92.25%, and 87.88% for one to five persons respectively.

articleTitle: Sentiment Classification of Multi-modal Memes Using Deep Learning and Transformer Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The widespread use of social media has elevated memes to a powerful mode of online communication. However, their misuse can fuel negativity and harm individuals’ mental health. Recognizing the sentiment of memes has become a challenge due to their multi-modal nature. This study proposes a method for sentiment analysis of Bengali memes, leveraging the concepts of multimodality. We investigated various deep learning techniques (CNN and BiLSTM) for textual features (ResNet50, VGG16, and VGG19) for visual features, as well as transformer techniques (m-BERT, XLM-R, and Bangla-BERT for textual features, and Vision Transformer and ConvNeXT for visual features). By combining image and text, our ConvNeXT+m-BERT model Proved highly effective, attaining an impressive f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-score of 0.712. Our proposed model (ConvNeXT+m-BERT) showed the highest performance on the ‘MEMOSEN’ [1] dataset compared to previous models. In a world where memes wield significant influence, our approach offers a crucial step toward understanding and managing their impact on digital conversations and mental well-being.

articleTitle: An Explainable AI Approach to Predicting Psychoactive Drug Consumption in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: According to the unpredictable as well as lethal nature of drugs, forecasting psychoactive drug consumption poses an enormous challenge to law enforcement authorities tasked with maintaining public safety. This study aims to address this issue by leveraging machine learning techniques to predict drug usage among the population of Bangladesh. Data was collected from 1,938 participants via a Google form, encompassing a wide range of demographic and behavioral information. We employed a variety of supervised learning models, including Gaussian Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest, Decision Trees, Ada Boost, Ridge Classifier, Logistic Regression, and a Voting Classifier. Our analysis focused on ten different categories of drugs—alcohol, nicotine, mushrooms, chocolate, heroin, cocaine, benzodiazepines, caffeine, LSD, and ecstasy—performing separate classifications for each. Notably, the prediction model for chocolate consumption demonstrated an exceptional accuracy rate of 98.97%, utilizing a combination of Logistic Regression and SVM. Additionally, to enhance the interpretability of our predictive models, we incorporated the Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) technique.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing the Usage of Artificial Intelligence among Bangladeshi Professionals: Mediating role of Attitude Towards the Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This study investigates the factors influencing the usage of artificial intelligence (AI) among Bangladeshi professionals, with a focus on the mediating role of attitude towards technology. The purpose is to enhance understanding of AI adoption using elements from the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). A quantitative research design was employed, utilizing a questionnaire distributed to 490 professionals, resulting in 190 usable responses. Data were analyzed using SmartPLS to assess the relationships among performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, attitude towards technology, and behavioral intention to use AI. The findings indicate that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, and perceived usefulness significantly influence AI adoption. Social influence and perceived ease of use exhibit mediated effects through attitude towards technology. The research is limited by its use of convenience sampling and a single-country focus, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The study's practical implications include guiding policymakers and industry leaders in designing targeted strategies to promote AI adoption among professionals. Social implications highlight the importance of addressing social factors and perceived ease of use to foster positive attitudes towards AI. This research contributes originality by integrating UTAUT and TAM models in a developing country context, providing nuanced insights into AI adoption among professionals. Future research should explore AI adoption across different developing countries and consider longitudinal and qualitative studies for a deeper understanding of technology adoption dynamics.

articleTitle: Construction Site Risk Reduction via YOLOv8: Detection of PPE, Masks, and Heavy Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Ensuring worker safety at construction sites is an increasingly significant issue for numerous construction businesses. Wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as masks, hard hats, hard shoes, and using equipment like excavators and trucks can effectively minimize injuries to workers at construction sites. However, it is important to note that safety hardhats and PPE are not always worn correctly for a variety of reasons. Therefore, the implementation of a computer vision-based automated safety helmet and personal protective equipment (PPE) detection system is of utmost significance. Several researchers have created detection systems using machine and deep learning techniques. However, only a handful have specifically concentrated on detecting helmets, while others have focused on detecting personal protective equipment (PPE) in construction sites. This study introduces a real-time computer vision system based on the You Only Look Once (YOLO) algorithm. The system is designed to automatically recognize Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), masks, hard hats, hard shoes, excavators, and trucks on a construction site. The YOLOv8 architecture is characterized by its high-speed performance, capable of processing 40-155 frames per second. This makes YOLOv8-based designs suitable for real-time object identification applications. The proposed method has independently created a dataset consisting of 1026 photos together with their corresponding label files. The dataset was subsequently split into a ratio of 64:12:24 (%) for training, testing, and validation, respectively. The experimental results demonstrated that the YOLOv8 architecture attained a mean average precision (mAP) of 95.4% for Mask, 82.1% for Excavator, 83.8% for Hard hat, 80% for Truck, 75.2% for No hardhat, 55% for PPE, and 54.8% for No_PPE. Consequently, it demonstrates exceptional performance in identifying Hard hat, PPE, Mask, and other items even in situations with limited lighting.

articleTitle: Measuring the Influence of Brand Image on Consumer Behavioral Intentions by using AI: Exploring the Mediating Role of Trust
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This study investigates the influence of various dimensions of brand image—perceived brand quality, brand loyalty, brand awareness, perceived value, brand personality, and brand communication—on consumer behavioral intentions, with trust acting as a mediating factor. Using survey data from 130 respondents and employing structural equation modeling (SEM) via Smart PLS, the research finds that brand loyalty, awareness, perceived value, personality, and communication significantly impact consumer intentions. Notably, trust mediates the relationships between perceived value and consumer intentions, and between brand communication and consumer intentions. However, perceived brand quality shows no direct impact on consumer intentions. The study acknowledges limitations such as convenience sampling and self-reported data, suggesting avenues for future research to enhance generalizability through diverse samples and longitudinal studies. Practical implications suggest that marketers should focus on strengthening these brand dimensions to build consumer trust and drive favorable behaviors, thereby potentially enhancing brand reputation and societal well-being. The study contributes to theoretical advancements by emphasizing trust as a pivotal mediator in brand-consumer relationships, offering valuable insights for strategic brand management in competitive market environments.

articleTitle: Prediction Hepatitis C Virus and Classifier Blood Donor and Disease using an Ensemble Approach in the Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Hepatitis C, caused by the hepatitis C virus, is a liver condition that can lead to severe complications if left untreated. The disease progresses through different stages, and while it is more easily treatable in the early stages, reaching the final stage without proper treatment makes recovery much harder, often resulting in high costs and significant pain. The current research emphasizes the importance of early detection as a simple and effective way to manage the condition. This study focuses on accurately predicting hepatitis C status, categorizing individuals as either blood donors or affected by the disease, using an ensemble machine learning approach. The research utilizes thirteen attributes and classifies the target into five categories: Blood Donor (including Blood Donor and Suspect Blood Donor) and Disease (encompassing Hepatitis, Fibrosis, and Cirrhosis). Several machine learning algorithms are employed, includeincludeing Decision Tree, K-nearest neighbor, Random Forest, and a Stacking Classifier. Among these, the Stacking Classifier outperformed the others, achieving an accuracy of 99.4%, precision of 99.7%, recall of 97.7%, and an F1-score of 98.7%.

articleTitle: Robotics in Animal Behavior Studies: Technological Innovations and Business Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Robotics and the study of animal behavior are complementary fields that cannot be separated. Animals have acquired inherent benefits in movement, thinking, processing information, and managing tasks as a result of extensive evolutionary processes. Biomimetic robots, designed with biological traits, significantly enhance their motor skills, cognitive functions, and control mechanisms, outperforming traditional robots. The progress in biomimetic technology, coupled with the unique interactive features of these robots, advances the study of animal behaviors. This research aims to offer a detailed review of the use of artificial intelligence and robotics, highlighting the intersection between robotics technology and animal behavior studies. The importance of mimicking animal behaviors in creating biomimetic robots is emphasized, with a focus on three key areas: movement behaviors, cognitive behaviors, and neural processes. The study explains the advantages of using biomimetic robots to understand animal behaviors, considering the animals' behavioral responses, group behavior patterns, and cognitive neurological activities. Additionally, the paper examines the potential applications of robotics in evaluating animal behavior and discusses the future developments in biomimetic robots and animal behavior research.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-Based Solution for Securing Central Bank Bond Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The management of central bank bonds faces significant challenges, including security vulnerabilities, inefficient processes, and the need for enhanced regulatory compliance. Traditional systems are unable to address these issues effectively, leading to potential risks and inefficiencies. There is a critical need for a solid and transparent system to secure and streamline bond management operations. To address these challenges, we propose a blockchain-based framework for securing central bank bond management. In this paper, we have designed and implemented a comprehensive blockchain infrastructure utilizing Smart Contracts, Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), and a Proof of Authority with Sharding and Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PoA-SBFT) consensus mechanism. We integrated FHE into the Microsoft SEAL library to ensure secure data exchanges and developed customized smart contracts to manage transactions and regulatory compliance. Our result analysis demonstrates significant improvements in transaction throughput and latency, indicating the system’s effectiveness and stability under various conditions.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Based Approach to Classify Tense from English Text
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This paper investigates the classification of tense in English text using machine learning algorithms. Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB), Decision Tree (DT), XGBoost, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) are the six classifiers used in the study. The dataset was collected from diverse sources including novels, books, blogs, articles, social media platforms, newspapers, websites and some of them self-made. The data underwent preprocessing steps such as cleaning, normalization, and feature extraction using TfidfVectorizer. Among the other algorithms, SVM achieved the highest accuracy at 97.17%. Classifier performance was assessed with metrics such as F1-score, recall, accuracy, and precision. To evaluate performance, ROC curves, and confusion matrices were also examined. The study underlines the necessity for focused approaches and draws attention to the significant gaps in the field of natural language processing (NLP) regarding tense classification studies. By leveraging machine learning, this research aims to enhance the accuracy and contextual appropriateness of tense classification, thereby improving cross-cultural communication and understanding in machine translation systems. This research contributes to NLP by offering a robust approach to tense classification and demonstrates the potential of SVM in achieving high accuracy for this task. Future work will focus on addressing limitations such as short training data, overfitting and tense conversion.

articleTitle: Automated Exam Script Checking using Zero-Shot LLM and Adaptive Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The manual grading of exam scripts is a labor-intensive process, often plagued by subjectivity and inconsistency. This study presents an innovative approach to automating the evaluation of exam scripts using the Large Language Model (LLM) integrated with Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) and Generative AI. Our system leverages the capabilities of GPT-4 to generate and evaluate answers, applying similarity measures to ensure accuracy and fairness in grading. The model’s adaptability through ZSL allows it to assess new questions without additional training. The system also incorporates iterative refinement techniques to enhance the quality of standard answers over time. Performance evaluations demonstrate a low error rate, with an average relative error of 1.29% for annotated questions and 1.67% for non-annotated questions compared to human graders. The performance underscores the automated system’s transformative potential in revolutionizing educational assessments, offering a consistent, fair, and highly efficient alternative to traditional grading methods.

articleTitle: Enhancing Breast Cancer Image Analysis through Attention Mechanisms: A Comparative Study of U-Net and Attention U-Net Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of mortality among women worldwide, underscoring the urgent need for enhanced diagnostic tools to facilitate early detection and treatment. Recent advancements in convolutional neural network (CNN) models have shown promise in categorizing breast cancer using image datasets. Traditionally, researchers have approached cancer diagnosis through Segmentation and classification as separate tasks, each with inherent limitations. This paper addresses these challenges by integrating deep learning models for simultaneous categorization and Segmentation of breast cancer. For classification tasks, we employed ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, VGG-16, and a modified Attention U-Net, optimizing their capabilities for accurate disease categorization. In parallel, we used U-Net and Attention U-Net architectures to precisely segment breast cancer tissues from medical images. Our research demonstrates that the Attention U-Net model surpasses other architectures, achieving exceptional results with 100% classification accuracy and 98% segmentation accuracy. These findings highlight the efficacy of integrated deep-learning approaches in advancing breast cancer diagnosis and treatment.

articleTitle: Wind Power Forecasting Using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Wind power forecasting is decisive for the incorporation of wind energy into the power grid, as it enables wind farms to optimize their operational efficiency and contributes to maintaining grid stability. This study evaluates three deep learning models namely Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and a Hybrid Model that integrates both architectures—for forecasting short-term wind power at the London Array wind farm, one of the largest wind farms in Europe. The LSTM and GRU models achieved root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 43.90 and 44.06, respectively, whereas the Hybrid model demonstrated a significant improvement with an RMSE of 38.28. Regarding mean absolute error (MAE), the LSTM model recorded a value of 26.32, the GRU model 25.60, and the Hybrid model further enhanced performance with an MAE of 21.90. The R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> metric was recorded at 0.97 for LSTM and 0.96 for GRU models, while the Hybrid model attained an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value of 0.97, indicating a strong fit for all models in capturing the variance in wind power data. These results demonstrate the efficacy of these deep learning models in precise wind power forecasting, offering benefits like enhanced grid stability, economic advantages through efficient energy market participation, and potential reductions in consumer energy prices, highlighting the models' applicability in the renewable energy sector.

articleTitle: Detecting and Understanding Cyberbullying in Bengali: An Explainable AI Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The internet, a global platform for communication, knowledge sharing, and social interaction, is increasingly marred by the pervasive threat of cyberbullying. This study presents a comprehensive approach to detecting cyberbullying in Bengali text. By consolidating existing datasets, incorporating feature engineering, and leveraging various machine learning and deep learning models, we aim to address this critical issue. To differentiate between general and specific types of cyberbullying, two datasets—binary-class and multi-class—are created. Using TF-IDF and Word2Vec vectorizers, alongside a diverse range of machine learning and deep learning models, we achieve top accuracies of 75.33% for the binary-class dataset and 93.16% for the multi-class dataset. To enhance interpretability, LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) is employed for local, instance-based explanations, while SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) provides global insights, highlighting the contribution of each feature to the model’s overall predictions. By analyzing randomly selected texts, we gain valuable insights into the reasons behind model predictions, particularly in cases of misclassification. This study contributes to a deeper understanding of cyberbullying and facilitates the development of more transparent and accurate detection systems for the Bengali language.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Bengali Sentiment Exploration Using Transformer Block I and Transformer Block II
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: The internet is responsible for the constant modernization of the planet. Anything is visible to everyone on social media. We work with sentiment or opinion mining in this study. Sentiment comes in two flavors: good sentiment and bad emotion. Moreover, there are numerous works in several languages, but the amount of work in Bengali emotion is restricted by the use of transformers. As a result, we concentrate on transformer blocks I and II's Bengali sentiment investigation. We gather information from Kaggle using the following datasets: Bengali Review (dataset 3), Conversion (dataset 2), and Predict Unsupervised (dataset 1). There are 19600 Bengali feelings in total. Various transformer techniques, include a lite Bert for self-supervised learning, a distilled version of BERT (DistilBERT), and bidirectional encoder representation from transformer (BERT). We employ long-short-term memory (LSTM), gated recurrent units (GRU), and recurrent neural networks (RNN) as examples of deep neural networks. While all the datasets function well and efficiently, the Bengali Review dataset with Transformer II operates at a very high speed. This is demonstrated by the following metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Roc score are 93.91% in LSTM with DistilBERT, 97.43% in LSTM with ALBERT, 97.15% in LSTM with BERT, 95.77% in LSTM with DistilBERT, and 93.41% in LSTM with ALBERT, respectively. Sentiment analysis greatly benefits from error exploration. The model functions more effectively when there are fewer mistakes. The LSTM using DISTILBERT yields the following error values: Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Mean Square Log Error (MSLE), respectively: 0.060, 0.246, and 0.029." All things considered; transformer block II offers the finest analysis.

articleTitle: An Explainable Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Transparent Deep Learning in the Classification of Eye Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Significant global health issues are posed by eye illnesses, especially in poor nations with inadequate financial and technological resources. Recent advances in pattern recognition for medical diagnosis have increased accuracy, but consistent health data collection and Artificial Intelligence integration are critical for Machine Learning model reliability. Explainable AI has made expert-level evaluation critical in sensitive areas. This study uses a hybrid approach to provide accurate categorization of eye diseases by utilizing deep learning assisted by Explainable Artificial Intelligence. The key contributions include using a Sequential Convolutional Neural Network to categorize eye disease images, significantly boosting accuracy with pre-trained CNN models, and employing the Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations method for clear result interpretations. The study compares two experimental models, a black-box CNN model and a glass-box model using XAI algorithm LIME. While pre-trained models like Inception V3 and Xception showed training accuracies of 81.5% and 85.5% and validation accuracies of 78.8% and 73.8%, respectively, the sequence model obtained training accuracy of 80.48% and validation accuracy of 76.34%. When combined with LIME, these pre-trained models showed increased interpretability providing thorough insights into disease prediction. Future research can be done on improving the effectiveness of AI-driven ophthalmic decision-making by comparing pre-trained models and XAI algorithms and experimenting with different CNN architectures.

articleTitle: An efficient Manuka honey purity classification technique with FSVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Manuka honey is renowned for its exceptional medicinal properties in healing wound infections and other conditions. Due to its high cost, this honey is a common target for fraud. Several machine-learning techniques are available for classifying the quality of Manuka honey. However, existing methods often struggle with accurate categorization. Imprecise data, high dimensionality, imbalances in various classes, and lengthy processing times are the root causes of misclassification. This research addresses these issues by providing a viable honey impurity classification method using Fuzzy Support Vector Machine (FSVM). The experiments utilize a freely available pre-processed Manuka honey dataset containing 3300 data points and 128 features. FSVM enhances the classification process by assigning fuzzy membership functions to each class, thereby handling imprecise data and resolving class imbalance problems. Furthermore, this study aims to minimize time and space complexity by reducing dimensions. For this purpose, four feature reduction techniques have been applied to the dataset, and the results have revealed that applying FSVM along with Class Embodiment Autoencoder (CEAE) has yielded 97% accuracy and F1 score. Lastly, a comparative analysis has been performed with other existing SVM methods, and it has been found that the proposed technique has outperformed previous SVMs in terms of accuracy and time and space complexity. The previous method takes (O(N!)) time complexity whereas the proposed method’s time complexity is (O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)), where N represents the number of data points in the dataset. This significant reduction provides a clear picture of the feasibility of the suggested approach and its potential to enhance the procedures involved in the classification and authentication of honey.

articleTitle: Yoga Posture Image Classification Using Big Transfer(BiT)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Yoga, celebrated for its holistic well-being approach, has become widely popular, providing both physical and mental benefits. Integrating technology, particularly deep learning models for yoga posture classification, has introduced innovative avenues for improved learning experiences. This paper explores the application of the cutting-edge Big Transfer model to classify yoga posture images. BiT, recognized for its exceptional performance in visual recognition tasks, leverages pre-trained representations to achieve high accuracy, even with limited data. This study involves an extensive dataset encompassing diverse yoga postures and variations.This research uses fine-tuned BiT model on this dataset and rigorously evaluate its performance. The results underscore BiT’s effectiveness in accurately identifying yoga postures, making it a valuable tool for automating posture assessment and providing real-time feedback during yoga sessions. Furthermore, the potential transformative applications of this technology in remote yoga instruction and telehealth is discussed. Automatic classification of yoga postures enhances personalized guidance and broadens access to yoga instruction. In conclusion, this paper presents a novel approach to yoga posture image classification using Big Transfer Model, with great results of 80.00% & 98.83% training accuracy & 69.14% & 95.69% validation accuracy in provided datasets respectively.BiT has the potential to revolutionize how practitioners learn and instructors teach yoga in the digital age. This research bridges the gap between technology and tradition, enhancing the practice of this ancient art.

articleTitle: Strategies for Effective Malware Analysis and Detection Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This research explores the issues that modern digital environments face due to advanced and widespread malware. The study focuses on issues related to feature selection, model efficiency, and the effectiveness of machine learning algorithms in categorizing Android malware because it acknowledges the drawbacks of conventional detection techniques in keeping up with the rapid evolution of threats. The main goals are identifying malware features, and creating optimized machine-learning models like Lightgbm, Xgboost, Decision-Tree, Random-Forest, etc. for real-world deployment. This study has achieved early successes in precise model development, significant feature identification, and optimization for a balanced accuracy-efficiency by utilizing the dataset, feature extraction, and cross-validated machine learning algorithms. Notably, the introduction of the HybridVRKD machine learning approach in this research lays the foundation for future developments in the field of cybersecurity making a significant contribution to threat identification. In every category, the Hybrid-VKRD model demonstrated 98% improved accuracy, making it the top performer.

articleTitle: Segmentation and Classification of Skin Lesions Using Ensemble of Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This research proposes an advanced ensemble model based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) designed to enhance the segmentation and classification of skin lesions, a critical step in the early detection of melanoma and other skin cancers. The study explores ensemble strategies, including bagging, boosting, and stacking, to identify the most effective approach for combining multiple CNN models. A novel ensemble method incorporating pre-trained dual encoders is introduced to improve segmentation accuracy by extracting critical features and precisely delineating lesion boundaries. The dual encoders are configured with different encoder-decoder architectures, activation functions, and optimization algorithms to optimize feature extraction and segmentation performance. The suggested model was tested on the ISIC 2019 and HAM10000 datasets, attaining an accuracy rate of 95.3%, with sensitivity at 93.7%, specificity at 96.8%, and an F1-score of 94.5%. The findings demonstrate a significant improvement over current leading techniques, confirming the robustness and reliability of the proposed ensemble strategy. The superior performance of the model suggests its potential for integration into clinical practice, providing dermatologists with a valuable tool for early skin cancer detection and improving patient outcomes through timely intervention.

articleTitle: Enhancing Skin Disease Classification Using LIME and Weighted Average Ensemble Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Skin diseases (SD) include a broad spectrum of skin-related problems, such as cancer, autoimmune diseases, and infections. They can manifest as rashes, bumps, discoloration, or changes in texture, often requiring precise diagnostic methods for effective management. Timely and efficient treatment of skin diseases depends on an accurate diagnosis. This study introduces a weighted ensemble model designed to enhance the diagnostic accuracy of various skin conditions, specifically classifying eight different categories. The model combines multiple classifiers to boost predictive performance, achieving remarkable results: 99% precision, 99% recall, and an F1 score of 99%. Additionally, it attained an overall accuracy of 99%, a Cohen's Kappa of 99%, and a minimal Hamming loss of 0.012.We used LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) to offer clear insights into the model's predictions, helping to explain how the model makes its decisions. LIME promotes transparency and aiding clinical decision-making in dermatology. These interpretable models allow practitioners to understand which features are most influential in diagnosing specific skin conditions. These results indicate a highly reliable system that could significantly support clinical decision-making in dermatology.

articleTitle: Advancing Medical Imaging: High-Performance Brain Tumor Detection and Classification Using Deep Learning and Grad CAM Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: An essential component of the diagnostic and treatment process is identifying brain tumors early in their onslaught. Traditional approaches struggle with processing sequential data and face limitations in maintaining computational efficiency with large-scale data. The pre-trained model has the advantage of eliminating computational complexity and processing the data very well. This research intends to improve the overall accuracy and robustness of the brain tumor detection and classification system, which is an amalgamate of several CNN-based pre-trained models for classification and two well-known detection models, Mask RCNN and YOLOv8, for tumor detection. The ResNet50 model delivers remarkable results, with an accuracy of 98.21% and precision of 97.32%. On top of that, it has a recall of 97.09% and an F1 score of 97.01%. The detection approach successfully pinpoints the tumor and offers a confidence score for detected regions exceeding 0.8. It also makes a highly accurate distinction between positive and negative tumors. The findings showcase significant benefits for medical imaging, offering enhanced interpretable results through the use of Grad CAM as the optimal classifier.

articleTitle: Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Fruit Detection from Bunch of Papaya Fruits with Complex Background
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Modern agriculture relies on the accurate detection and counting of fruits to ensure precise crop estimates, optimize resource use, and boost overall productivity. In this paper, we focus on developing a lightweight deep-learning model for detecting green papaya fruits, that is practical and convenient for farmers. For any categorization task, a well-structured dataset is indeed necessary. However, no suitable dataset is available for papaya detection or counting. We capture real-time data from the field under various conditions (background, lighting, overlapping), annotate the data, and make a well-structured dataset to open a new direction in fruit counting research, especially on papaya counting. Green papaya counting is a challenging task because it blends in with foliage due to its color. Where the images contain overlapping instances and complex backgrounds, we need high-level features to discriminate them. To address this, we propose a CNN-based robust object detection architecture. We employ five one-stage object detection models (YOLOv8n, YOLOv8s, YOLOv8m, YOLOv8l, and YOLOv8x) and a two-stage object detection model (Faster R-CNN) to observe the accuracy. We aim not only to improve papaya production but also to offer a new research direction applicable to other fruits with similar detection challenges and downstream tasks. We want to suggest an ideal model through which farmers can calculate real-time yields with smartphones. By analyzing the experimental results, we propose YOLOv8m model for this problem in terms of a good trade-off between accuracy and model complexity.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Approaches to Unmasking Fake News: A Simple Comparison of ML and DL Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: False news spreads quickly due to the extensive distribution of incorrect or misleading information across digital channels, which is a global problem. This bias undermines the credibility of information, promotes the spread of misleading information. Utilizing machine learning and deep learning models this study examines the detection of inaccurate information. Natural Language Processing methods are used for data preprocessing on the text datasets. Five machine learning models are used in this study: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, and Passive Aggressive Classifier. After preprocessing, the accuracy values of these models are 95%, 99.7%, 99.3%, 98.9%, and 99.5%, respectively. The study demonstrates that the decision tree model has superior performance, with the LSTM algorithm following closely after. The PAC and LSTM model have also demonstrated commendable results of 99.5% accuracy. The accuracies offer valuable information regarding the constraints of each model, aiding researchers in selecting suitable ways for identifying counterfeit news. The findings assist individuals in making informed decisions on the establishment of precise and effective ways for identifying false information, which is essential to maintaining the integrity of information distribution.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Enhanced Stock Market Prediction with Fine-tuned Technical Indicators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Since stock data is unpredictable, noisy, and fluctuating, it is critical to analyze and predict it. Traditional statistical models struggle with the high volatility and multifaceted nature of the market, influenced by diverse factors such as economic indicators, investor behavior, company performance, and global events. Machine learning, particularly deep learning techniques like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), have shown promise in improving predictive performance. Reinforcement learning (RL) methods, including model-based, off-policy, and actorcritic, further enhance predictive capabilities by adapting to changing environments and maximizing rewards. This study aims to build a profit/loss RL model with unique indicator values to improve RL models' efficacy and precision in trend detection and data testing within the stock market. The methodology involves analyzing various stock datasets using five RL algorithms: Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C), Deep Q-Network (DQN), Actor-Critic using Kronecker-Factored Trust Region (ACKTR), Proximal Policy Optimization 1 (PPO1), and Proximal Policy Optimization 2 (PPO2). The study incorporates hyper-tuned technical indicators to optimize RL algorithms' performance. Upon training and evaluation, Deep Q-Network (DQN) outperforms the other algorithms, demonstrating its suitability for the stock market's dynamic and unpredictable nature. The datasets include historical price data and technical indicators.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Mycology: Transfer Learning for Automated Mushroom Species Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Mushroom categorization is a difficult process since there are so many different species and they all have different aesthetic qualities. In this paper, we are to investigate the use of transfer learning techniques for precise mushroom classification. We have examined the performance of EfficientNetB0, ResNet50, InceptionV3, and MobileNet, four well-known transfer learning models. The mushroom dataset is first preprocessed to make sure that the images are properly scaled and normalized. After initializing and fine-tuning the pre-trained weights of the above-mentioned models on our mushroom dataset, we then apply transfer learning techniques. Each model is trained using a carefully chosen training set, and its performance is assessed using a different test set. Our findings reveal that all four transfer learning models successfully categorize mushrooms, achieving outstanding classification accuracies. With a 97% accuracy rate, EfficientNetB0 surpasses the other models when we compare them. Its sophisticated design, which combines compound scaling and AutoML approaches to attain the best accuracy and efficiency, is responsible for its exceptional performance. The results of this study demonstrate the value of transfer learning in tasks involving mushroom categorization. Additionally, they stress the benefit of using cutting-edge models like EfficientNetB0, which produce greater accuracy compared to conventional transfer learning architectures. The development of automated methods for mushroom identification and subsequent breakthroughs in the mycology field can be facilitated by the use of these findings by academics and professionals working on mushroom classification.

articleTitle: From Social Media to Mental Health Insights: A Hybrid CNN-LSTM Model for Depression Detection in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Depression, a pervasive mental disorder, significantly impacts individuals' daily lives, manifesting as persistent sadness, a negative disposition, lack of interest or pleasure, feelings of guilt or worthlessness, and sleep disturbances. Advances in psychological methodologies, including the use of questionnaires and the analysis of social media posts, have facilitated the detection of individuals affected by this mental health issue. While mental health is a priority in many developed countries, it remains primarily neglected in regions like Bangladesh. This neglect is evident in the lack of a standardized corpus for detecting depression in the area. In this paper, we present the annotated data collected by our crawlers and detail the processes undertaken to standardize this corpus. We also propose a novel model for depression analysis and detection, which integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Our model achieves an accuracy of 90.11%, demonstrating its efficacy. Additionally, we compare the proposed model with various machine learning models, including SVM, Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, KNN, AdaBoost, CNN, LSTM, and Decision Tree with hyperparameter tuning, using several performance metrics to highlight the advantages of our approach.

articleTitle: Diabetes Prediction: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms with SMOTE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This paper conducts a comprehensive investigation into diabetes prediction utilizing diverse machine-learning algorithms, including Random Forest, Ada Boost, Gradient Tree Boosting, Gaussian Naive Bayes, SVM, and KNN. The principle goal is to identify the best and sustainable algorithm for diabetes prediction by evaluating their performance on a dataset of 100,000 samples. Predictor attributes encompass gender, age, BMI, hypertension, smoking history, etc. Performance evaluations employed a 5-fold cross-validation method. Due to class imbalance, a Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was implemented for classifier training. The best performance was achieved using SMOTE and the Gradient Tree Boosting classifier, attaining an accuracy of 96.99%, precision of 91.99%, recall of 70.76%, and F1 score of 79.975%. This proposed approach demonstrates significant advancement in diabetes prediction, contributing valuable insights for optimizing machine learning models in healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Techniques for Early Brain Tumor Detection: A Comparative Study on Models Performance Utilizing Dataset Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Brain tumor is one of the most common reasons for death in all ages of people. Brain tumor occurs when abnormal growth of malignant cells is formed within the brain. Early detection of brain tumor using image classification can accelerate the treatment process and avoid the challenge of survival. The performance of image analysis techniques is often degraded due to poor visibility of images. Enhancing such images significantly improves not only the image visibility but also the deep learning-based image classification. This study focuses on the in-depth experiment over the MRI brain image dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, pituitary gland tumors, and healthy brain images. A considerable improvement in tumor detection has been observed after performing some image enhancement techniques. Three deep learning models, EfficientNetB0, MobileNet V2, and ResNet50, are used in the experiment. The obtained result shows that EfficientNetB0 and ResNet50 performed better than MobileNet V2. After enhancement, the accuracy of Efficient-NetB0, ResnetNet 50 is 91. 73%, 90. 59% respectively. It can be stated that image enhancement can considerably improve the performance of the deep learning models to identify early brain tumor diseases.

articleTitle: Vegetable Classification using Deep Learning: Insights from Transfer Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Deep learning models for vegetable classification address a key demand in current agricultural and food sector activity. The significance of precisely recognizing and categorizing vegetables is multifaceted, ranging from agricultural process optimization to food safety and quality management. Deep learning models for vegetable classification meet a major demand in the agriculture and food industries, providing considerable gains in efficiency, production, and innovation. The present research aims to employ deep learning techniques to accurately categorize vegetable images. In this regard, the focus of this research is to discover whether conventional CNN architectures—such as VGG16, ResNet50, MobileNetV2, DenseNet121, VGG19, Xception will perform best in terms of accuracy and efficacy when applied to newly gathered image datasets. Vegetable Image Dataset of 21,000 images split into 15 categories. Our work into vegetable classification demonstrated the capabilities of six different deep learning models. With accuracy scores ranging from 98.23% for the Xception to an astonishing 99.97% for DenseNet121, each model brought its own capabilities to the table. In addition, the accuracy of ResNet50 was as high as 99.73%, second only to MobileNetV2 and DenseNet121 which achieved the results at a rate of 97.88% respectively Although, the models which stood out from others were VGG16 and vgg19 with accuracy as 99.53% and 99.13%, followed xception based model giving an accuracy of 98.23%.

articleTitle: Dropout Prediction of University Students in Bangladesh using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: A significant concern in universities is student dropout, which reflects the institution's quality and affects its reputation and the students' future careers. High dropout rates can directly impact a private university's budget, marketing strategy, and sustainability. Therefore, it is crucial to improve the quality of higher education, reduce student dropout rates, and enhance academic planning. Analyzing dropout patterns is essential for effective management. This study aims to predict dropout rates of university student in Bangladesh by using various machine learning techniques. In order to create a machine learning model for forecasting the dropout rate of students, we used seven well-known classifiers: SVM, KNN, XGBoost, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes, and Random Forest. The dataset included around 500 Bangladeshi university students who answered 29 questions. The collection comprises records with different properties. After preprocessing, the data were split into two sets: one for training and the other for testing. The classifiers were subsequently trained and tested. To identify the most suitable classifier for this problem, we thoroughly assessed the performance of all seven classifiers. Our findings indicate that XGBoost and Random Forest have 98.06% accuracy rate which is highly promising for predicting dropout rates. By utilizing machine learning to predict university dropout rates, early intervention, more effective resource allocation, and enhanced student support are made possible, which in turn improves retention rates, academic results and can be useful for developing the education system in the university of Bangladesh.

articleTitle: A Comparative Behavioral Analysis of ASD Kids Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition that affects various aspects of individuals' social interactions, communication, learning, and behavior. While ASD can manifest at any stage of life, symptoms typically emerge within the initial two years. Timely identification of autism can greatly influence the effectiveness of its intervention and treatment. This study centers on identifying distinct characteristics that facilitate the automation of the ASD diagnostic process. Additionally, it aims to assess and conduct a comparative examination of different machine learning algorithms such as Decision Tree (DT), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), Logistic Regression (LR), Gradient Boosting (GB), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), an Ensemble Model (EM), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Random Forest (RF) in order to forecast the likelihood of autism disorder. Most importantly four different behavioral datasets following Autism-Spectrum Quotient (AQ-10) screening tool are normalized and merged which consisting of 3492 records, facilitates the development of robust machine learning models to predict the likelihood of ASD. Different performance metrics like; accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Specificity and ROC-AUC are employed to make a better comparison of the mentioned algorithms.

articleTitle: Enhancing Bangla Sign Language Recognition with Max Voting Ensemble
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Sign language plays a vital role in facilitating communication for individuals with hearing impairments. While substantial research has been dedicated to the recognition of sign languages such as English and Arabic, Bangla Sign Language (BdSL) remains underexplored presenting challenges in model generalization and performance. This study introduces an innovative approach that leverages the Max Voting Ensemble Technique to enhance the accuracy and generalizability of BdSL recognition models. By integrating multiple pre-trained deep neural networks including Xception, InceptionV3, MobileNetV2, DenseNet121 and ResNet50 our method addresses the limitations of existing systems. The proposed ensemble model significantly improves performance achieving validation accuracies of 98.10% and 95.93% and test accuracies of 99.99% and 96.38% on the BDSL49 and BdSL-38 datasets respectively. These results underscore the model’s potential for real-world applications offering a robust framework for advancing BdSL recognition and supporting the development of accessible communication tools.

articleTitle: Leveraging Sequential Deep Learning Models for Detecting Multitude of Human Action Categories
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In today’s world, where science and technology are constantly evolving day by day, people are drawn to tangible experiences and visual representations. There’s a growing effort to teach machines about human movements and postures to enable smart decision-making. This has led to increased interest in the field of human action recognition (HAR) among researchers globally. Our research focuses on implementing advanced technologies to address criminal activities, specifically emphasizing Human Activity Recognition (HAR). Moreover, our dataset includes 1275 videos, covering 20 different actions involving both violent and non-violent behaviors. In addition, we have developed a pipeline that utilizes YOLO-v8 to extract background, followed by models for accurate video classification. two models, conv-lstm and lrcn, were incorporated into our deep learning pipeline. Through our observations, we found that the LRCN model outperformed the other model, achieving an accuracy of 62% and an F1 score of 60% for the 20 classes, for 17 classs an accuracy of 63% and an F1 score of 66%. for binary classifcation LRCN got accuracy of 88% and an F1 score of 87%Our research focusses the potential of advanced technologies to significantly improve Human Activity Recognition (HAR) in addressing various aspects of criminal activities in real-time scenario. This marks a substantial step forward in intelligent decision-making and public safety.

articleTitle: Empowering Limited Data Domains: Innovative Transfer Learning Strategies for Small Labeled Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Traditional Indian Medicine faces the risk of extinction due to insufficient transfer of knowledge. This research highlights the critical need for preservation through modern technology and techniques. It addresses the challenges of limited labeled data by employing pioneering transfer learning approaches for classifying Indian Medicinal Plants, specifically leaves. The study utilizes diverse trained models and a bespoke model tailored for this task, systematically investigating transfer learning dynamics to mitigate issues such as overfitting and underfitting in neural network training. Rooted in Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) concepts, the research demonstrates how transfer learning enhances neural network efficiency, especially when labeled data is scarce. Practical application is illustrated with a dataset of plant images, providing a real-world context for evaluating transfer learning strategies. By leveraging models trained with large data in relevant domains, the research facilitates effective feature extraction and generalization despite limited labeled data. A significant contribution of the research is the comparison of outcomes from various models with the proposed custom CNN model, HerboraNet, which achieves a remarkable accuracy of 95%. This research underscores the superiority of transfer learning over training models with limited input, particularly in data-constrained domains, highlighting its pivotal role in enhancing model efficiency and adaptability.

articleTitle: Integrated Multiclass Sentiment Analysis of Movie Reviews: Combining Fine-Tuned DistilBERT, LightGBM and XAI for Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Sentiment analysis of movie reviews plays a critical role in understanding audience perspectives and predicting trends in the entertainment industry. This work presents an integrated approach that encourages a fine-tuned DistilBERT model for feature extraction, followed by LightGBM for classification, and SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) for model interpretability. By combining these advanced techniques, our approach achieves a high accuracy of 97%, significantly outperforming traditional methods. The use of DistilBERT enables precise contextual understanding of textual data while offering a more efficient and lightweight alternative to the full BERT model. LightGBM provides efficient and scalable classification, and SHAP ensures transparent and interpretable model decisions, allowing us to understand key factors driving sentiment predictions. This integrated framework enhances accuracy and also provides valuable insights into the model’s behavior, making it a robust tool for sentiment analysis in movie reviews.

articleTitle: Analyzing Schizophrenic Texts From Social Media Through Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Schizophrenia is a destructive personality disorder where people may develop harmful symptoms if not diagnosed promptly. The research focuses on identifying language patterns indicative of schizophrenic-prone texts in online communication and intends to contribute to the development of early intervention techniques in mental health using ML and NLP methods. The study has utilized an existing dataset to examine language patterns associated with schizophrenia in social media posts. Various ML, BERT and RNN models have been used to predict textual data suggestive of schizophrenia. The analysis shows excellent results, with the DistilBERT achieving the highest accuracy rates of 97%, GRU acquiring 91% accuracy, and the logistic regression achieving 93% accuracy respectively.

articleTitle: Improving Bangla Regional Dialect Detection Using BERT, LLMs, and XAI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: This research addresses the challenge of identifying and categorizing Bangla regional dialects through the application of sophisticated natural language processing techniques. Automated translation, digital content personalization, and speech recognition systems are all improved by precise dialect detection, which is a result of the linguistic diversity in Bangladesh. Few-shot learning techniques were used to compare the performance of transformer-based models, specifically Bangla BERT, with state-of-the-art large language models such as GPT-3.5 Turbo and Gemini 1.5 Pro, and to fine-tune them. The methodology entailed the utilization of a diverse regional Bangla speech samples from the Vasantor dataset, which encompassed regions including Mymensingh, Chittagong, Barishal, Noakhali, and Sylhet. In order to enhance the interpretability of the model, implementation of Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) was done. The Bangla BERT model achieved the highest accuracy of 88.74%. GPT-3.5 Turbo’s few-shot learning exhibited substantial potential, with an accuracy rate of 64%. These results underscore the significance of hyperparameter optimization and fine-tuning in the enhancement of regional dialect detection models.

articleTitle: Fraud Detection with Ensemble Learning and Web-Based Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In the ceaseless battle against digital fraud, our fraud detection project emerges as a proactive and comprehensive response to the audacity of fraudsters who pilfered millions, showcasing the urgency to fortify defenses. Navigating the intricacies of big data, we harness the power of advanced Machine Learning, deploying a squad of eight classification models to combat the ever-evolving tactics of fraud. With an unwavering commitment to understanding the complexities of fraudulent activities, our objective is crystal clear: to contribute a high-performance fraud detection model. Facing the challenge of imbalanced data, we embark on a journey of exploration, identifying, and implementing resampling methods that significantly enhance the model’s efficiency. The crescendo of our efforts culminates in the deployment of a robust ensemble model, led by the exemplary Voting Ensemble, now accessible through a user-friendly website. This project not only achieves its core objectives but establishes a sustainable and efficient solution for real-world fraud detection, deftly bridging the gap between cutting-edge research and practical, impacting application.

articleTitle: Bengali Text Classification: Distinguishing Saintly and Common Forms using Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: In the realm of AI technological advancements, Natural Language Processing (NLP) stands out as a branch dedicated to enhancing machine or system processing of human language tasks. Text classification, a crucial area within NLP, has significantly fortified natural language processing tasks. This study zeroes in on language processing tasks in Bengali, our mother tongue. Notably, there's a dearth of research on Bengali text classification, especially concerning its two linguistic forms: "saint" (Sadhu bhasa) and "common" (Cholito bhasa), with a limited dataset size available. Thus, this study aims to classify Bengali texts based on these two forms, utilizing around 2948 pieces of data gathered from Bengali literature, blogs, and articles. To classify Bengali texts, various supervised machine-learning algorithms have been employed, including MNB, RF, DT, SVM, KNN, and XGB. Before implementing these algorithms, dataset preprocessing techniques were applied, such as primary cleaning, regular expression removal, stopwords removal, digit removal, null value removal, and tokenization. Among all the applied machine learning techniques or classifiers for predicting texts in the two forms—saint and common—SVM achieved the highest output accuracy of 92.33%. Additionally, RF, XGB, MNB, DT, and KNN attained accuracies of 91.87%, 91.20%, 88.04%, 86.68%, and 84.88%, respectively. Ultimately, this study opens up avenues for further research in Bangla language processing, particularly in the realm of text classification.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework for Disaster Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Twitter is a website for social networking and news delivery that has significant importance at the time of any disaster by providing valuable information related to the disaster. The analysis of social media has become crucial in monitoring and gathering important information during disasters, including reports on the impact of the event, as well as updates on injuries and damage to infrastructure. This information is valuable for disaster management teams in their response efforts. During a disaster, an automated system that can retrieve relative information and massive Twitter data could help disaster relief volunteers complete their duties efficiently amidst the chaos. The majority of researchers use a unimodal (only images or text) approach. The use of a single modality (text or images) frequently results in the loss of important insights. Though some of the researchers used a multimodal approach to classify the disaster types, most of the works were based on the pre-trained CNN model for example VGG16, and InceptionV3 for image classification which can lead to vanishing gradient problem, and the CNN or RNN-based model for textual analysis, which does not work for longer input sequences and is not focused on a critical part of the text, then combining these two models to classify the six different damage types. In our proposed model, we have used a multi-head attention-based pre-trained BERT model for text feature extraction which works on long input sequences and also gives attention to the specific portion of the text, and the ResNet50 model for image features extraction which addresses the vanishing gradient problem. Then we used an early fusion approach to concatenate these two networks followed by the soft-max classifier. We are able to achieve 93.16% weighted F1 score in classifying different damage types.

articleTitle: Comprehensive biomarkers analytics web API reveals Comorbidities between Obesity and Skin Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Obesity, characterized by excess body fat, is commonly associated with various diseases, including skin cancer. Despite extensive research, the intricate relationship between obesity and Skin cancer disorders remains underexplored. Our study aimed to elucidate the diseasome, comorbidities and shared molecular mechanisms between obesity and Skin cancer disorders using comprehensive bioinformatics analysis. Leveraging large-scale gene-expressed datasets from those tissues that are affected by these conditions, we integrated data from Gene Ontology (GO) and molecular pathways, employing Gene Set Enrichment Analysis to uncover semantic similarities between shared genes and GO terms. Our findings reveal that obesity and skin cancer share altered gene expression suggesting interconnected disease mechanisms. We developed a bioinformatics pipeline using R and Python libraries, culminating in a web application that visualizes these connections and features a search bar for identifying gene-disease associations. This application is reusable and adaptable, allowing researchers to input new data and uncover disease interactions. The web application, pipeline codes, and database with CI/CD integration are accessible by the obes-skin.onrender.com subdomain. The application includes bioinformatics charts, graphs, semantic similarity matrices, and a Venn diagram tool that works by uploading CSV files with specific genes or gene lists, offering a deeper understanding of disease interaction mechanisms.

articleTitle: Triple Attention MobileNetV3: Harnessing Integrated Attention and Transfer Learning for Next-Generation Skin Lesion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Detecting skin lesions, especially cancerous melanoma, early is vital for effective treatment. However, traditional detection methods are costly, time-consuming, and involve numerous tests, making early detection challenging. This study introduces a new approach called Triple Attention MobileNetV3 (TAMN), which utilizes a novel multi-stream attention-infused Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture based on Transfer Learning principles. TAMN aims to improve skin lesion recognition, offering a potentially more efficient solution. Data augmentation and careful dataset splitting addressed class imbalance, preventing biased modeling. This TAMN architecture integrated an Attention Module comprising Channel Attention, Squeeze and Excitation Attention, and Soft Attention mechanisms to emphasize crucial features and regions relevant to accurate classification. Gradient Class Activation Map (Grad-CAM) visualization identified areas the model focused on, improving interpretability and explainability. The proposed model achieved 99.56% accuracy on the PAD-UFES-20 dataset, outperforming the direct use of any pre-trained models. The attention modules significantly boosted metrics like precision, recall, F1-score and specificity compared to baselines, showcasing their efficacy in enhancing skin lesion classification for early cancer detection. The approach demonstrates the potential of attention-based deep learning models for accurate and interpretable skin lesion analysis, paving the way for improved early screening and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Amplifying Maximum Power Point Tracking in Solar PV Charge Controllers Using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Solar Photovoltaic (PV) systems suffer from fluctuating power output due to variations in temperature of operation and light irradiation. Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controllers are activated to maximize energy harvest regardless of these changes. This research examines fuzzy logic control (FLC) for MPPT in solar PV charge controllers. Fuzzy logic, with its ability to represent complex relationships through linguistic expressions, offers distinct advantages. It can effectively manage the non-linearities present in PV systems without requiring intricate mathematical models. The proposed fuzzy logic MPPT controller continuously monitors the output power of PV and its rate of change concerning voltage. MATLAB optimization will be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed Fuzzy Logic MPPT controller in conjunction with a DC-DC buck converter. This converter significantly improves the impedance matching between the solar panel and the battery. By dynamically modifying the duty cycle of getting signals in response to the voltage and current reading from the solar panel, the buck converter improves power transfer efficiency. This ensures that the battery stores the maximum amount of electricity the solar panel produces. To measure the possible increases in power extraction efficiency, the performance will be compared to well-established MPPT approaches. MATLAB optimizations are used to assess the performance of fuzzy logic MPPT controllers and compare them to traditional MPPT techniques. The research paper seeks to demonstrate how FLC can improve the effectiveness of power extraction and improve the overall performance of the solar PV system.

articleTitle: Predicting Heart Failure Survival: A Machine Learning Approach with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Heart failure is one of the global health issues that is needed for precise prognostic instruments. In order to predict survival and time-to-event outcomes in patients with heart failure, this study assesses machine learning techniques. Most effective prediction models are determined for heart failure prognosis by combining clinical information and evaluating model performance. According to the results, the LightGBM classifier had the lowest accuracy at 77%, while the SVM classifier had the highest accuracy at 88%. These findings suggest that machine learning can greatly improve clinical judgement in cardiovascular medicine and advance patient-focused treatment.

articleTitle: Cyberbullying Detection: An Innovative MultiTask Learning Framework for Analyzing Harmful Memes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Cyberbullying encompasses bullying behaviors on digital platforms, including spreading false information, sharing embarrassing content, sending threats, or impersonating others to send harmful messages. This study delves into the growing problem of cyberbullying, focusing on the spread of damaging memes on social media. The research explores the potential of hybrid models for detecting cyberbullying memes. This hybrid model combines elements from some existing multitask learning frameworks: MultiAchiever and CentralNet, DMTL and MTEIR, MTEIR and MTLAttention, DMTL and MTLAttention, as well as DMTL and MoE. By leveraging these frameworks, the study investigates the effectiveness of these hybrid approaches in analyzing memes for characteristics associated with cyberbullying, including harmfulness score, sentiment analysis, sarcasm detection, and target identification. The research explores the use of advanced pre-trained models for both image and text feature extraction. A comprehensive dataset consisting of 6,006 memes with textual annotations is used to train and evaluate the models. This nuanced analysis aims to contribute to a more sophisticated understanding of online memes and enhance content analysis capabilities, ultimately fostering safer digital spaces. Furthermore, among all the hybrid models, The MultiAchiever-CentralNet algorithm, in conjunction with ResNet50 and DistilBERT for image and text feature extraction, outperforms existing models with a notable accuracy of 68.64% with f1_score of 65.54%.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of ML Techniques for Predicting Diabetes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic illness that is common around the world, impacting millions of people and creating serious problems for public health. To avoid complications and enhance patient outcomes, diabetes must be identified early and managed well. We report a thorough investigation of the use of ML methods for forecasting diabetes in this publication. We utilize the Diabetes Dataset for Pima Indians (PIDD), a reputable industry benchmark dataset, for our analysis. Our study begins with data preprocessing steps, including addressing missing values, encoding categorical variables, and scaling features. Subsequently, we partition the dataset into sets for testing as well as training to ensure the robustness of our models. We evaluate a range of techniques for ML, such as LR, RF, GB, KNN, SVM, ANN, DT, LSVM, and NB, for their effectiveness in predicting diabetes. A variety of metrics for performance, such as F1-scoring, accuracy, recall, and precision are used to assess every framework once it has been assessed on the testing set after being trained on the training set. Furthermore, we conduct a comparative analysis of the models, considering factors such as interpretability, complexity, and generalization ability. Our results show promising performance across several ML models, with NB and LR exhibiting particularly high accuracy and precision in predicting diabetes. These findings underscore the potential of ML techniques in facilitating early detection and personalized management of diabetes, thereby contributing to improved patient outcomes and healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: Seeing the World in Dots: A Machine Learning Adventure in Colorblind Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Computing, Applications and Systems (COMPAS)
abstract: Color is a vital communication element, conveying the message’s meaning and differentiating the contents. Nevertheless, color vision deficit (CVD), called colorblindness, affects 8% of the global population. This impairment alters color perception, making reading and understanding the message difficult. This issue becomes increasingly significant with the expanding accessibility of multimedia content in digital environments, including web browsers, digital images, entertainment media, and social media. One of the methods of identifying CVD is the Ishihara Color-blind Test. Ishihara images consist of a red-green background and a hidden number. Color-blind persons won’t recognize the number as they cannot recognize the red and green colors. Using color glasses or contact lenses this deficiency can be overcome. The main point is that there is no cure for this deficiency. This research explores machine learning's potential to overcome this challenge.
